definition_zh: 抢救；打捞；挽救（局面、声誉等）；海上救助；从废墟中收出的可用东西
definition_en: to save something from a disaster, shipwreck, or loss, or to rescue whatever value is left when a situation has gone badly wrong
core_image: 风浪里伸出钩爪，把沉在海底的船货一点点拖回岸边
scene: 暴雨过后，仓库里一片狼藉，工人们还在泥水里翻找。The crew tried to salvage the machinery from the flooded basement.
sceneCN: 这里 salvage 是「抢救、挽救」（第 1 个义项：在灾祸或困境中把东西救出来）；句意为工人设法把机器从被淹的地下室抢出来。图中可辨识物件：泥水、机器、绳索。

pos.zh: 动词：抢救；打捞；挽救（局面等）
名词：抢救；海上救助；打捞上来的财物；（难以挽回时的）补救

collocations.zh: 打捞权；救助费用请求权

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可救的；可挽回的」
由本词加后缀 -er 构成，义为「打捞者；救捞人员」
与本词同出拉丁语 salvare「拯救」，义为「拯救；得救」
与本词同源，义为「救星；救世主」

senses.title: To save property from disaster
senses.definition: to save goods, machinery, or buildings from damage after a flood, fire, or other disaster
senses.definitionCN: 在洪水、火灾等灾害后抢救出货物、机器或房屋
senses.example: Volunteers salvaged furniture from the burning house.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者从起火的房子里抢救出家具。
senses.why: Salvage is the noun salve borrowed from the sea, where people were paid for saving a ship and its goods; the verb simply names that rescue.
senses.whyCN: salvage 原本是从海上借来的名词 salve，指有人因救助船只与货物而得到报酬；动词不过把这次救援说出来。

senses.title: To raise goods from a wreck
senses.definition: to recover a ship, its cargo, or lost objects from the bottom of the sea or from deep water
senses.definitionCN: 从海底或深水中找回船只、货物或失物
senses.example: Divers salvaged two bronze cannons from the wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员从沉船中打捞起两门铜炮。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the sea trade of raising a lost ship and its cargo; the hook that drags cargo up from the deep is the core image.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项正是打捞沉船与货物的海上营生；把货物从深处拉上来的钩爪就是核心意象。

senses.title: The reward and right to save
senses.definition: the payment and legal right given to those who rescue a ship or its cargo at sea
senses.definitionCN: 在海上救助船只或货物时应得的报酬与法律权利
senses.example: The tug company claimed salvage after guiding the trawler to port.
senses.exampleCN: 拖船公司在把拖网渔船领回港口后提出了救助费用要求。
senses.why: For centuries salvage named the reward paid for a rescue at sea, so the same word still names the legal right and the fee.
senses.whyCN: 几个世纪里 salvage 都指海上救助所得的报酬，所以这个词至今仍兼指法律权利与费用。

senses.title: Things saved from a wreck
senses.definition: the goods, parts, or materials recovered from a wreck, a fire, or a ruined place, often sold or reused
senses.definitionCN: 从沉船、火灾或废墟中收回的货物、零件或材料，常被出售或再利用
senses.example: The yard sells salvage from old ships to builders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家船厂把从旧船上打捞的材料卖给建筑商。
senses.why: What is dragged up has to be named too; this sense is the total of saved things rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: 被拉上来的东西也需要一个名字；这个义项指的是救出的全部物品，而不是动作。

senses.title: To rescue a situation or reputation
senses.definition: to rescue what can still be saved from a failing plan, company, match, or public image
senses.definitionCN: 从失败的计划、公司、比赛或公众形象中救出还能保住的成分
senses.example: A late goal salvaged a point for the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 临近结束的一个进球为客队挽回了积分。
senses.why: When a project is like a sinking ship, only part of it can be brought ashore; to salvage is to take that part with you.
senses.whyCN: 项目像一条将沉的船时，只有一部分能被带回岸上；salvage 就是把那一部分带走。

senses.title: To use the remains
senses.titleCN: 废物利用；从残骸中取用
senses.definition: to take usable parts or materials from something old, broken, or abandoned and put them to new use
senses.definitionCN: 从旧的、坏的、废弃的东西上取下可用的部件或材料并加以利用
senses.example: Old window frames were salvaged for the restoration.
senses.exampleCN: 旧窗框被拆下来用于修复工程。
senses.why: Salvage treats the wreck as a store of parts: the hull is gone, but the fittings still have work to do.
senses.whyCN: salvage 把残骸看作一堆零件：船体没了，但配件还能继续派上用场。

senses.title: A final saving act
senses.definition: a last attempt that saves only part of what was at risk, often after most of the loss has already happened
senses.definitionCN: 事后做出的最后挽救，往往只能保住风险中的一部分，损失多半已经发生
senses.example: The emergency loan was a salvage of an already broken budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔紧急贷款只是对已经亏空的预算做的最后一救。
senses.why: Salvage never promises a whole ship; it promises only what the hooks can still reach and raise.
senses.whyCN: salvage 从不承诺完整的船，只承诺钩爪还能触到并拉上来的东西。

intro.en: Salvage is a sea word borrowed from French and Latin: it first named the reward for saving a ship, then saving the ship itself.
intro.cn: salvage 是从法语和拉丁语借来的航海词：先指救助船只所得的报酬，后来才指救援本身。

items.en: Latin salvare meant to save or keep safe, from salvus, safe and sound. The deeper root is generally reconstructed as Proto-Indo-European *solwo-, whole and unharmed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 salvare 意为「拯救、保住」，来自 salvus「安全、完好」。更早的词根一般认为可重构为原始印欧语 *solwo-「完整、未受伤害」。

items.en: In medieval Latin and maritime custom, salvagium named the payment given to those who rescued a vessel in peril. The exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语与海事惯例中，salvagium 指救助遇险船只所得的报酬。确切的首见用法不确定。

items.en: Old French salvage carried the maritime sense of rescue and its fee into English after the Norman Conquest.
items.cn: 诺曼征服之后，古法语 salvage 带着海上救援与救助报酬的含义进入英语。

items.en: The English noun is recorded in the sixteenth century for the saving of goods and ships; insurance and admiralty law gave it a technical edge.
items.cn: 英语名词在十六世纪有记载，指抢救货物与船只；保险法与海事法庭赋予它专门术语的地位。

items.en: The verb appears later, growing from the technical noun, and the abstract sense of salvaging a reputation or a season spread into ordinary speech.
items.cn: 动词出现得较晚，是从这个专业名词生长出来的；挽救声誉或赛季之类的抽象用法也进入了日常口语。

items.en: Modern use adds recycling signs such as a salvage shop and abstract rescue phrases such as salvage a bad day.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了循环利用的含义，如 salvage shop「废品回收店」，也增加了抽象挽救的说法，如 salvage a bad day「挽回糟糕的一天」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the Latin saving root; the near-meaning group gathers rescuing and recovering words with different forces.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「拯救」词根的词；近义组收救援与收回类的词，力度与色彩各不相同。

entries.definition: the act of being saved from harm or loss, and in religion, deliverance from sin; it is the abstract result of saving.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拯救、得救」，宗教里也指「灵魂得救」，是拯救的抽象结果。

entries.definition: a person who saves someone from danger or ruin; the same Latin root lost its l and the v shifted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「救星、救世主」，同出拉丁语词根，拼写上丢了 l 并改动了 v。

entries.definition: a soothing ointment for a wound, and figuratively anything that comforts; it comes from the same Latin healing word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「药膏」，比喻指「安慰」，与 salvage 同出一语源。

entries.definition: able to be saved from a disaster or a failure; formed from salvage plus the suffix -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可救的、可挽回的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: fierce or wild; it merely sounds close and comes from Latin silvaticus, of the woods, with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「凶猛的、野蛮的」，只是读音相近，词源不同，出于拉丁语 silvaticus「树林中的」。

entries.definition: to get people out of danger; it usually names saving lives, while salvage usually names saving goods.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「营救、救援」，通常多指救人，而 salvage 多指抢救财物。

entries.definition: to get back something lost, such as a sunken object or money; it focuses on getting it back, not on the danger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「找回、收回」，如捞回沉没物或追回款项，强调取回，而不强调危险。

entries.definition: to bring something back from where it was lost or stored; neutral in tone and often used for data and files.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取回、检索」，语气中性，常指取回文件与数据。

entries.definition: to get something back that was taken or lost, and in formal writing to make good a loss; it lacks the wreck and hook picture of salvage.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取回、收回」，正式语体中也指「弥补损失」，但没有 salvage 那种残骸与钩爪的画面。

entries.definition: to bring something back to its former good condition; it works on the thing itself rather than pulling it out of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修复、恢复」，作用于事物本身，而不是把它从危险里拉出来。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin saving root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「拯救」词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Salvus is safe: salvage always means something is being kept safe from ruin.
normal.cn: salvus 意为「安全的」：salvage 里的东西总是在被保下来，免于毁坏。

normal.en: A salvage operation is the practical scene: cranes, divers and hooks at work after a disaster.
normal.cn: salvage operation 是最具体的画面：灾后吊车、潜水员与钩爪齐上阵。

normal.en: Salvage rights are the maritime fee claim, a reminder that the word began at sea.
normal.cn: salvage rights 指海事救助费用的请求权，提醒人这个词起步于海上。

normal.en: Salvage value is what a wrecked thing is still worth to someone.
normal.cn: salvage value 指毁坏之物对别人仍有几分价值。

normal.en: Compare rescue: rescue saves people, salvage saves property and what can still be used.
normal.cn: 对比 rescue：rescue 多救人，salvage 多救物以及还能利用的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a hooked crane rising from dark water with a crate clamped in its jaws.
abstract.cn: 想象带钩的吊臂从昏暗的水中升起，爪子夹着一只木箱。

abstract.en: Imagine a diver swaying beside a broken hull, cutting a hatch free and pushing it upward.
abstract.cn: 想象潜水员在断裂的船体旁摇晃，把舱盖割下来往上推。

abstract.en: Think of a team pulling planks out of a burnt shed, because each side wall is still good.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人从烧毁的棚屋里拆木板，因为每块侧板还能用。

examples.en: Firefighters salvaged the paintings before the roof collapsed.
examples.cn: 消防员在屋顶塌落前抢救出了那些画。

examples.en: The salvage operation recovered nearly all of the ship cargo.
examples.cn: 这次打捞行动找回了船上几乎所有货物。

examples.en: The coach hoped to salvage the season after two early defeats.
examples.cn: 两次早早失利之后，教练仍希望挽救这个赛季。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「筛了我」——把沉船里的货筛一遍，把还能用的捞上来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 salvus「安全的、完好的」→ salvare「拯救」→ 中世纪拉丁语 salvagium「海上救助及报酬」→ 古法语 salvage → 英语 salvage。核心是「把还能救的东西保住、捞上来」。

sensesIntro.en: Salvage starts in a sea trade of reward for rescuing a ship, then narrows into raising goods, then widens again into saving whatever a disaster or failure leaves standing.
sensesIntro.cn: salvage 起于「救助船只换报酬」的海上营生，先收窄为打捞货物，再扩展到从灾难或失败中保住剩下的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hook is lowered from a boat and drags a crate up from the dark water.
core.cn: 核心意象：钩爪从船上垂下，把木箱从暗水里拉上来。

branches.en: On land, the same saving act protects property from fire and flood.
branches.cn: 在陆地上，同样的救援动作保护财物免于火灾与洪水。

branches.en: The maritime core: raising a wreck, the fee and right to do so, and the goods that come up.
branches.cn: 海上核心线：打捞沉船、据此取得报酬与权利，以及被捞上来的货物。

branches.en: The metaphor of a sinking project lets salvage mean rescuing a reputation or a match.
branches.cn: 项目将沉的比喻让 salvage 可以指挽救声誉或一场比赛。

branches.en: Taking usable parts from ruins is the wreck seen as a store of still useful material.
branches.cn: 从废墟中取用可用部件，是把残骸看作仍有用的材料库。

branches.en: Both the plain rescue and the last-ditch one only promise what can still be reached.
branches.cn: 普通抢救与最后一救都只承诺还能触到的那部分。

intro.en: Salvage is built on the Latin adjective salvus and the verb salvare; English adds suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: salvage 建立在拉丁语形容词 salvus 与动词 salvare 之上；英语再用后缀扩展出这个词族。

latinIntro.en: The recorded Latin words salvus, salvare, salus and salvator show the saving root clearly, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的拉丁语词 salvus、salvare、salus 与 salvator 清楚显示「拯救」词根，只有更早的印欧语形式属于重构。

items.example: Salvus supplies the image of something kept whole.
items.exampleCN: salvus 提供「保持完好」的意象。

items.example: Salvare is the saving verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: salvare 是这个词族背后的「拯救」动词。

items.meaning: payment for a rescue at sea
items.example: Salvagium gives the maritime sense.
items.exampleCN: salvagium 提供海上救助的含义。

items.example: Salve keeps the healing colour of the root.
items.exampleCN: salve 保留了词根的「医治」色彩。

items.meaning: rescue of goods, and its fee
items.example: Salvage joins rescue and reward.
items.exampleCN: salvage 把救援与报酬合在一起。

items.example: The suffix -age forms salvage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 构成 salvage。

items.example: The suffix -able forms salvageable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 salvageable。

items.example: The suffix -er forms salvager.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 salvager。

items.example: Salvageable describes what can still be saved.
items.exampleCN: salvageable 描述还能被救回来的东西。

items.meaning: a person who does salvage work
items.example: Salvager names the worker, not the act.
items.exampleCN: salvager 指做这项工作的人，而不是行为。

definition_zh: 疗养院；疗养地；（尤指旧时的）结核病疗养院；休养地
definition_en: a place, especially a quiet country home or clinic, where people go to recover from a long illness, above all tuberculosis
core_image: 山坡上的白色疗养楼，长窗敞开，病人躺在露台的躺椅上慢慢呼吸
scene: 山里的空气又干又清，窗外是松林，病人每天要在长廊上晒太阳。In those years, a long stay in a sanatorium was the best hope for a weak lung.
sceneCN: 这里 sanatorium 是「疗养院」（第 1 个义项：供病人长期休养的疗养机构）；句意为在那些年里，去疗养院长期休养是肺弱病人最大的指望。图中可辨识物件：松林、长廊、躺椅。

pos.zh: 名词：疗养院；疗养机构；休养地

collocations.zh: 供肺痨病人休养的疗养院

derivatives.zh: 借自拉丁语 sanitas 的另一种拼写，义为「疗养院；休养地」
与本词同出拉丁语 sanitas「健康」，义为「精神健全」
与本词同出拉丁语 sanitas，义为「卫生的；清洁的」
由 sanitary 加后缀 -ize 构成，义为「消毒；净化」
与本词同出拉丁语 sanus「健康的」，义为「神志正常的」

senses.title: A long-stay health institution
senses.definition: a residential institution where patients with a long illness stay for weeks or months in a quiet, healthy setting
senses.definitionCN: 供长期患病者在此住上数周乃至数月、环境安静适宜康复的居住式机构
senses.example: She spent a whole winter in the sanatorium above the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 她在湖边山坡上的疗养院住了一整冬。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -orium names a place, and sanare means to heal, so a sanatorium is literally a place for health.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -orium 表示场所，sanare 意为「治愈」，所以疗养院字面上就是「用来恢复健康的地方」。

senses.title: A tuberculosis home
senses.definition: a specialized institution where consumptive patients lived in dry mountain air, sunlight, and fresh food before drug cures
senses.definitionCN: 在药物问世前专门收治肺痨病人、让他们在干燥山间空气、阳光与优质饮食中休养的机构
senses.example: His grandfather was sent to a sanatorium in the Alps for rest and fresh air.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祖父被送到阿尔卑斯山的疗养院休养、呼吸新鲜空气。
senses.why: Before antibiotics, the only cure for tuberculosis was air, sun, food and patience, and the sanatorium was the building that organized them.
senses.whyCN: 抗生素出现之前，治肺结核全靠空气、阳光、饮食与耐心，疗养院正是把这些组织起来的建筑。

senses.title: A health resort
senses.definition: a town or district with mineral springs, mild climate, or clean air, visited by people who need rest and treatment
senses.definitionCN: 有矿泉、温和气候或清新空气的城镇或地区，供需要休养与治疗的人前往
senses.example: The village grew into a sanatorium for those who needed warm salt air.
senses.exampleCN: 那个村子逐渐发展为疗养地，吸引需要温暖带盐空气的人前来。
senses.why: The core place grew outward until the whole town counted as the healing setting, so a resort town could take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 核心的「场所」向外扩张，直到整座小镇都成了养病环境，于是疗养小城也能用同一个名字。

senses.title: A school or home for health
senses.titleCN: （旧时的）健康学校；疗养性收容所
senses.definition: an old-fashioned term for a boarding school or children home run on health lines, with outdoor sleep, light lessons and regular medical care
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用语，指按健康原则办的寄宿学校或儿童之家，主张户外睡眠、轻量课业与定期医疗照护
senses.example: The orphanage opened a sanatorium school where children slept on open porches.
senses.exampleCN: 孤儿院开办了一所健康学校，孩子们在露天的门廊上睡觉。
senses.why: In the age before drugs the same regime, light lessons, open air and supervised rest, was applied to children, so a school could also be a place for health.
senses.whyCN: 在药物出现以前，同样的养生安排，即轻课业、户外空气与有人看护的静养，也被用在孩子身上，于是学校也能成为「为健康而设的场所」。

senses.title: The idea of a healing place
senses.definition: any place that feels like a refuge where a tired or injured person, or a broken system, can heal
senses.definitionCN: 比喻任何像庇护所一样、能让疲惫或受创的人（乃至有问题的体系）得以复原的地方
senses.example: The quiet library became her sanatorium after a hard year.
senses.exampleCN: 艰难的一年后，那座安静的图书馆成了她的疗养之所。
senses.why: Once the disease sense faded, the picture of a quiet place that restores you stayed behind, and the word could be lent to any refuge.
senses.whyCN: 病院义淡去之后，「安静、能让你复原的地方」这个画面留了下来，这个词就可以借给任何庇护之处。

senses.title: An unhealthy place in jest
senses.definition: a place described by contrast as a place where people get sick rather than heal, used with irony about stressful settings
senses.definitionCN: 反讽用法，指那种非但不养人反而让人生病的地方，多用来形容高压环境
senses.example: He called the busy newsroom a sanatorium after a week without sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 连着一周没睡之后，他把忙碌的新闻编辑室称为疗养院。
senses.why: Every healing word can be turned on its head; calling a place that exhausts people a sanatorium rewrites the core image into its opposite.
senses.whyCN: 任何带「治愈」意味的词都可以被反过来用；把一个耗人的地方叫作疗养院，就是把核心意象翻转成反面。

intro.en: Sanatorium is a modern Latin invention, but it rests on the same healing root that gives sane, sanitary and sanity.
intro.cn: sanatorium 是现代拉丁语造出来的词，但它立在与 sane、sanitary、sanity 相同的「健康」词根上。

items.en: Latin sanus meant healthy or sound, and sanare meant to heal. The verb sanare produced sanator, a healer.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sanus 意为「健康的、完好的」，sanare 意为「治愈」；动词 sanare 又生出表示「医治者」的 sanator。

items.en: The suffix -orium names a place for an activity, as in auditorium or dormitory, so sanatorium means a place for healing.
items.cn: 后缀 -orium 表示进行某种活动的场所，如 auditorium、dormitory，所以 sanatorium 意为「用来康复的地方」。

items.en: Early modern writers used sanatorium for a place of cure, often in a broad, almost literary sense; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 近代早期的作者用 sanatorium 指「治病之处」，含义往往宽泛甚至带文学色彩；确切的首见使用不确定。

items.en: With the tuberculosis sanatorium movement, the word took its best-known shape: mountain air, verandas and forced rest.
items.cn: 随着结核病疗养院运动的兴起，这个词定下了最广为人知的形态：山间空气、露台与强制静养。

items.en: American usage spread the variant sanitarium, which is modeled on Latin sanitas but does not follow the Latin -orium rule.
items.cn: 美国用法流行起 sanitarium 这一变体；它模仿拉丁语 sanitas，却不符合拉丁语 -orium 的构词规则。

items.en: Once antibiotics made long stays unnecessary, the word moved from medicine toward resort, retirement home and figurative refuge.
items.cn: 抗生素使长期休养不再必要之后，这个词从医学用语转向度假地、养老院与比喻性的庇护所。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built on Latin sano, save and heal; the near-meaning group gathers places and cures for rest and recovery.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 sano「治愈」构成的英语词；近义组收休养与康复类的场所与疗法。

entries.definition: connected with keeping places clean and free from disease; it shares the Latin health word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「卫生的、清洁的」，与疗养院共享拉丁语「健康」一词。

entries.definition: the condition of having a healthy mind; it comes from the Latin noun sanitas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「心智健全」，来自拉丁语名词 sanitas。

entries.definition: the American spelling for a health resort or rest institution; it is close to sanatorium but built on sanitas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，是美国拼写，义为「疗养院、休养地」；与 sanatorium 形近但仍属同一词族。

entries.definition: a substance that kills germs; it comes from the verb sanitize, built on sanitary.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消毒剂」，由 sanitary 衍生的动词 sanitize 而来。

entries.definition: a member of a senate; it looks close but comes from Latin senex, old man, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「参议员」，只是形近，词源不同，出于拉丁语 senex「老人」。

entries.definition: another name for the same kind of rest institution, common in American writing; the two words overlap almost fully.
entries.definitionCN: 同类休养机构的另一种叫法，在美国文献中常见，两词含义几乎完全重叠。

entries.definition: a place with mineral springs or water treatments for health; it is more about bathing than about treating disease.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「矿泉水疗养地」，偏重沐浴与理疗，而不是治病。

entries.definition: a place where people stay while recovering from illness or surgery; shorter stays and less medical control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「康复之家」，供病后或手术后的人休养，住得较短，医疗管理也较少。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin health root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「健康」词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Sanus is healthy: sanatorium, sane, sanity and sanitary all carry the same health root.
normal.cn: sanus 意为「健康的」：sanatorium、sane、sanity、sanitary 都带着同一个健康词根。

normal.en: The suffix -orium marks a place, just as it does in auditorium.
normal.cn: 后缀 -orium 表示场所，就像在 auditorium 里一样。

normal.en: A tuberculosis sanatorium was the mountain veranda, the sun and the enforced rest.
normal.cn: 结核病疗养院的核心就是山间露台、阳光与强制静养。

normal.en: The plural can be sanatoria or sanatoriums; both are accepted.
normal.cn: 复数既可写 sanatoria，也可写 sanatoriums，两种都被接受。

normal.en: The American spelling sanitarium belongs to the same family, though it follows sanitas.
normal.cn: 美国拼写 sanitarium 属于同一词族，只是跟的是 sanitas。

abstract.en: Picture a white building on a hillside with long open windows and figures in blankets on deck chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象山坡上一栋白色楼房，长窗大敞，披着毯子的人躺在躺椅上。

abstract.en: Imagine a bell that ends visiting hours, and the slow quiet that follows on the veranda.
abstract.cn: 想象一声铃响结束探视时间，随后露台上慢慢静下来。

abstract.en: Think of the mountain air itself being prescribed like a dose of medicine.
abstract.cn: 想象山间的空气本身就像一味药，被医生开成处方。

examples.en: He was cured of tuberculosis after a year in the sanatorium.
examples.cn: 在疗养院住了一年后，他的结核病痊愈了。

examples.en: The old sanatorium is now a hotel with a view of the lake.
examples.cn: 那所旧疗养院如今成了一家有湖景的旅馆。

examples.en: Sanatoria of the pines welcomed children with weak lungs.
examples.cn: 松林里的疗养院收留肺弱的孩子们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「山里头嘛」——山里头空气好，正适合下山去疗养，所以指的是疗养院；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sanus「健康的」→ sanare「治愈」→ 现代拉丁语 sanatorium（-orium 表场所，如 auditorium）→ 英语 sanatorium，字面即「治病养身之地」。

sensesIntro.en: Sanatorium begins as a general place for healing, becomes the mountain clinic for tuberculosis, widens into resort towns, and finally turns figurative.
sensesIntro.cn: sanatorium 先是泛指的治病之所，继而专指结核病山中诊所，又扩展到疗养地，最后生出比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white clinic on a sunny hillside with rows of deck chairs and open windows.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光山坡上的白色疗养楼，露台上摆着一排排躺椅，长窗大开。

branches.en: The plain sense: a residential institution for a long health stay.
branches.cn: 基本义项：供长期休养的居留式疗养机构。

branches.en: The tuberculosis chapter gave the word its defining picture of sun, air and rest.
branches.cn: 结核病这一章给了这个词最典型的画面：阳光、空气与静养。

branches.en: The institution leaks into the landscape: the resort town itself becomes the sanatorium.
branches.cn: 机构渗入地景：疗养小城本身也被称为疗养地。

branches.en: The old health-school sense shows how far the word once reached into education and child care.
branches.cn: 旧时的健康学校义项显示这个词曾延伸到教育与儿童照料。

branches.en: The modern figurative uses keep the healing refuge and its ironic reverse.
branches.cn: 现代的比喻用法保留了「治愈性庇护所」一端，也生出反讽的反面。

intro.en: Sanatorium joins a Latin healing root to a Latin suffix for places; English then builds sane, sanity, sanitary and sanitize around the same base.
intro.cn: sanatorium 把拉丁语「治愈」词根与表示场所的拉丁语后缀拼在一起；英语又围绕同一词基造出 sane、sanity、sanitary 与 sanitize。

latinIntro.en: Latin sanus, sanare, sanator and sanitas are all recorded, so the root is secure and only the modern Latin coinage is recent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sanus、sanare、sanator 与 sanitas 都有记录，词根确凿无疑，只有现代拉丁语的造词本身年代较近。

items.example: Sanus is the adjective behind the healing family.
items.exampleCN: sanus 是这一「治愈」词族背后的形容词。

items.example: Sanare supplies the action of healing.
items.exampleCN: sanare 提供「治愈」这一动作。

items.example: It marks sanatorium as a place of healing.
items.exampleCN: 它标明 sanatorium 是治病的场所。

items.example: The noun was coined for places of cure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是为治病之处而造的。

items.example: The ending makes the word a neuter noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使它成为中性名词。

items.example: Sanitarium is the American spelling variant.
items.exampleCN: sanitarium 是美国拼写变体。

items.example: Sanity keeps the Latin idea of soundness.
items.exampleCN: sanity 保留了拉丁语「完好」的观念。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms sanity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sanity。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms sanitary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成 sanitary。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms sanitize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 sanitize。

definition_zh: 圣所；圣殿；神圣之地；（尤指允许少数人进入的）私室、密室
definition_en: a very holy place inside a temple or church, or a private room where someone may not be disturbed
core_image: 神殿最深处的一间小屋，帷幕垂落，只有祭司能踏进去
scene: 古神庙的最里面隔着一间小屋，门帘厚重，寻常人只敢在门槛外张望。Only the high priest could enter the sanctum behind the curtain.
sceneCN: 这里 sanctum 是「圣所」（第 1 个义项：神殿或教堂内神圣的内殿）；句意为只有大祭司才能走进帘子后面的圣所。图中可辨识物件：石柱、门帘、灯火。

pos.zh: 名词：圣所；圣殿；私室；密室

derivatives.zh: 与本词同出拉丁语 sanctus，义为「神圣的；圣洁的」
与 sanctum 同根，由 sanctus「神圣的」加后缀 -ify 构成，义为「使神圣；使圣洁」
由 sanctify 加后缀 -ation 构成，义为「圣化；使圣洁」
与本词同根，由 sanctus 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「神圣性」
由 sacro 与 sanctus 组合而成，义为「神圣不可侵犯的」

senses.title: The holy inner place
senses.definition: the most sacred part of a temple or church, often closed off and entered only by priests
senses.definitionCN: 神庙或教堂中最神圣的部分，常常隔开，只有祭司才能进去
senses.example: The worshippers stood outside the sanctum and bowed.
senses.exampleCN: 信众站在圣所外躬身行礼。
senses.why: Sanctum is the neuter form of Latin sanctus, sacred, so the word names the space itself as set apart for the holy.
senses.whyCN: sanctum 是拉丁语 sanctus「神圣的」的中性形式，所以这个词把空间本身命名为「划出来献给神圣的地方」。

senses.title: The innermost room of all
senses.definition: the innermost sanctuary, as in the phrase sanctum sanctorum, the holiest place where the holiest of holies is kept
senses.definitionCN: 最深的圣所，见于短语 sanctum sanctorum，是供奉至圣之物的最神圣之处
senses.example: Beyond the second curtain lay the sanctum sanctorum.
senses.exampleCN: 第二道帘子之后就是至圣所。
senses.why: Latin built a superlative by repeating the word in the genitive, so sanctum sanctorum is holy of the holy and marks the deepest ring of the temple.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用属格重复来表达最高级，所以 sanctum sanctorum 就是「至圣者之圣」，标出神殿最深的一圈。

senses.title: A private room
senses.definition: a private, quiet room, especially a modern one such as a study or office, where a person does not want interruption
senses.definitionCN: 私密安静的房间，尤指书房、私人办公室等现代空间，主人不愿被打扰
senses.example: The editor only signs contracts in his own sanctum.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主编只在自己的私室里签合同。
senses.why: If a room is set apart and entered by few, the holy interior of a temple shades easily into the private inner room of a house.
senses.whyCN: 房间只要被隔开、少有人进，神庙的神圣内殿便顺势滑向宅子里那间私密内室。

senses.title: A protected area for someone
senses.titleCN: （某人的）专属领地；受庇护的一角
senses.definition: a special corner of a place that one person treats as theirs to think, work, or rest in without being moved
senses.definitionCN: 某处的一角，被某人视为专属用来思考、工作或休息，不容别人占据
senses.example: The corner of the library by the window was her sanctum.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆靠窗的那个角落是她的专属领地。
senses.why: The core image is a mark on the floor that outsiders cannot cross, and any corner that a person claims this way borrows the temple wall around it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是地上一条外人不得跨越的界线，任何被人这样认领的角落，都借来了神庙的那道围墙。

senses.title: An inner group
senses.definition: the small inner circle of a group or room from which most outsiders are kept out, as in the inner sanctum of a party
senses.definitionCN: 团体的少数核心成员圈，或外人很少进得去的内室，如政党的核心圈子
senses.example: The meeting was held in the inner sanctum of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在俱乐部的核心内室举行。
senses.why: The same spatial logic moves from a place to a people: the ring of few insiders is the innermost chamber of an organization.
senses.whyCN: 同一套空间逻辑从地方转到人身上：少数知情人围成的圈，就是组织的最内层。

senses.title: A place of refuge
senses.definition: a safe, quiet refuge where a person finds shelter, calm, or protection from a difficult world
senses.definitionCN: 安全安静的庇护之处，让人在艰难的世界里找到庇护与平静
senses.example: After a week of noise, the old garden was a sanctum of calm.
senses.exampleCN: 一周吵闹之后，那座老花园成了安歇之境。
senses.why: Set apart for the sacred also means set apart from harm, so the holy space becomes a safe one, and this is the sense the figure of speech keeps.
senses.whyCN: 划出来献给神圣，也意味着与伤害隔开，于是神圣的空间同时成为安全的所在，这正是比喻用法保留的那一层。

intro.en: Sanctum began as the sanctum sanctorum of Latin Bible translations, meaning holy of holies, and English kept the phrase and then shortened it.
intro.cn: sanctum 始于拉丁语圣经译本里的 sanctum sanctorum，意为「至圣所」，英语先借入整个短语，后来缩短成 sanctum。

items.en: Latin sanctus meant sacred, from the verb sancire, to make sacred or fix by law; sanctio named the ratifying decree.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sanctus 意为「神圣的」，来自动词 sancire「使神圣、依法确立」；sanctio 指确认的法令。

items.en: Jeromes Latin Bible used sancta sanctorum for the holiest room of the Temple, a literal rendering of the Hebrew holy of holies.
items.cn: 耶柔米的拉丁语圣经用 sancta sanctorum 指圣殿中最神圣的房间，是希伯来语「至圣所」的直译。

items.en: English took the phrase in its Latin form, sanctum sanctorum, meaning the inmost shrine; the shorter sanctum was used for a holy or enclosed place.
items.cn: 英语以拉丁语原形借入 sanctum sanctorum，意为「最内层的神龛」；较短的 sanctum 则用来指神圣或被隔开的地方。

items.en: Records of English sanctum in the secular sense are thin; the everyday phrase inner sanctum for a private office or inner group is generally dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 sanctum 作世俗义项的确切记录较少；inner sanctum 指私人办公室或核心圈子的常见用法一般认为出现在十九世纪。

items.en: Modern journalism and business writing widened inner sanctum into a mild cliché for any private room, boardroom or elite circle.
items.cn: 现代新闻与商业写作把 inner sanctum 推成了略带陈套意味的说法，泛指私人房间、会议室或精英圈子。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin sacred root sancire; the near-meaning group gathers sanctuaries, shrines and private refuges.
note.cn: 形近组收来自拉丁语神圣词根 sancire 的词；近义组收圣所、神龛与私密庇护所类的词。

entries.definition: to make something holy or to treat it as holy; it shares the Latin adjective sanctus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使神圣、使圣洁」，与 sanctum 共享拉丁语形容词 sanctus。

entries.definition: the quality of being holy or sacred; the noun of the same root, abstract rather than spatial.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神圣性、圣洁」，属同一词根的抽象名词，而非空间词。

entries.definition: too sacred or valuable to be changed or criticized; it joins Latin sacer and sanctus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「神圣不可侵犯的」，由拉丁语 sacer 与 sanctus 拼合而成。

entries.definition: to permit or approve, and a penalty meant to enforce a rule; it grew from the same verb of ratifying.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「批准」或「制裁」，与认证确立的同一动词同源。

entries.definition: showing that you feel morally better than other people; it shares the sacred root but turns it into a criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「伪善的、装圣洁的」，共享「神圣」词根，却把那层神圣变成了批评。

entries.definition: a holy place, and also a place of safety or protection, such as a refuge for wildlife; broader than sanctum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「圣所、庇护所」，也指自然保护区之类的安全处，范围比 sanctum 更宽。

entries.definition: a sacred place where a god or a saint is honored, often small; it is more about the object of devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神龛、圣地」，常指较小的崇拜场所，更强调供奉对象。

entries.definition: the innermost and most sacred room of the Temple, and by extension any very special inner space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「至圣所」，引申指任何极其重要的内层空间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin sacred root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「神圣」词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Sanctus is sacred: sanctum, sanctify, sanctity and sanctify all rise from the same word.
normal.cn: sanctus 意为「神圣的」：sanctum、sanctify、sanctity 都出自同一个词。

normal.en: Sanctum is the neuter form, so it means the holy thing or the holy place.
normal.cn: sanctum 是中性形式，所以指「神圣之物」或「神圣之地」。

normal.en: Sanctum sanctorum is the Latin doubling that marks the very inmost shrine.
normal.cn: sanctum sanctorum 是拉丁语的重复结构，标出最里面的圣所。

normal.en: Inner sanctum pairs the spatial inner with the sacred, and it is a fixed collocation.
normal.cn: inner sanctum 把「内里」和「神圣」配在一起，是固定搭配。

normal.en: The sanc- root also sits in sanction, where a rule is made sacred and binding.
normal.cn: sanc- 词根也出现在 sanction 里，那里指把规则定为神圣而有约束力的。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy curtain across a doorway and a lantern burning behind it in an empty stone room.
abstract.cn: 想象门口横着一道厚帘，帘后石室空荡，只有一盏灯亮着。

abstract.en: Imagine a visitor stopping one step before a line on the floor and never crossing it.
abstract.cn: 想象访客在地面的一条线前停下一步，始终不跨过去。

abstract.en: Think of a modern desk in a quiet room with the door shut and a small sign saying no entry.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里一张书桌，门关着，挂着一个小小的「勿入」牌。

examples.en: Only the priest dares to enter the sanctum of the old temple.
examples.cn: 只有祭司才敢走进这座古庙的圣所。

examples.en: The inner sanctum of the party was closed to reporters.
examples.cn: 该政党的核心圈子不对记者开放。

examples.en: He retired to his sanctum to finish the manuscript.
examples.cn: 他回到自己的私室去完成手稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「上刻它」——在神庙门上刻下禁忌，谁也不能擅入的圣所；这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sancire「使神圣、依法确立」→ sanctus「神圣的」→ 中性形式 sanctum「神圣之地」→ 短语 sanctum sanctorum「至圣所」→ 英语 sanctum（圣所；私室）。

sensesIntro.en: Sanctum starts as the sacred inner room, deepens into the holy of holies, then moves into private rooms, personal corners, inner circles and refuges.
sensesIntro.cn: sanctum 先是神殿的神圣内室，进而指至圣所，再扩展到私人房间、个人角落、核心圈子与庇护所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dark room at the heart of a temple, cut off by a heavy curtain.
core.cn: 核心意象：神殿中心一间昏暗的小屋，被厚重的帷幕隔开。

branches.en: The temple line: the holy inner room that priests alone may enter.
branches.cn: 神殿线：只有祭司能进入的神圣内室。

branches.en: The superlative line: the holy of holies marks the deepest, most sacred ring.
branches.cn: 最高级线：至圣所标出最深、最神圣的一圈。

branches.en: The private line: a study, an office or a claimed corner keeps the walls but loses the altar.
branches.cn: 私密线：书房、办公室或被人认领的角落保留了围墙，却不再有祭坛。

branches.en: The social line: the inner circle of a group takes over the innermost chamber.
branches.cn: 社交线：团体的核心圈子接过了最内层的内室。

branches.en: The protective line: set apart from the profane also means set apart from harm.
branches.cn: 庇护线：与凡俗隔开，也意味着与伤害隔开。

intro.en: Sanctum is a Latin participle-style adjective turned into a noun; English builds sanctify, sanctity and sanctify around the same sanct- base.
intro.cn: sanctum 是拉丁语形容词转为名词的结果；英语围绕同一 sanct- 词基造出 sanctify、sanctity 等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sancire, sanctus, sanctio and sanctitas are all recorded, so the root is secure; only modern English first dates for the private-room sense are uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sancire、sanctus、sanctio 与 sanctitas 均有记录，词根确凿；只有现代英语「私室」义的首见年代不确定。

items.example: Sancire is the act of setting something apart as sacred.
items.exampleCN: sancire 是把某物划出来定为神圣的行为。

items.example: Sanctus is the adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: sanctus 是这一词族的形容词。

items.meaningCN: 中性词尾，指神圣之物或之地
items.example: The neuter ending turns the adjective into a place noun.
items.exampleCN: 中性词尾把形容词变成场所名词。

items.example: Sanctum names the inner holy room.
items.exampleCN: sanctum 指内部的神圣房间。

items.example: Sanctio gives English sanction.
items.exampleCN: sanctio 给出英语 sanction。

items.example: Sanctitas is the abstract partner of the place word.
items.exampleCN: sanctitas 是场所名词的抽象对应词。

items.example: Sanctify applies the root as an action.
items.exampleCN: sanctify 把这个词根用作动作。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms sanctify.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 构成 sanctify。

items.example: Sanctity keeps the abstract sense.
items.exampleCN: sanctity 保留抽象含义。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms sanctity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sanctity。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms sanctification.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 sanctification。

definition_zh: 檀香木；檀木料；檀木树；檀香（香味）
definition_en: the sweet-smelling yellowish wood of a slow-growing tropical tree, used for incense, carving and perfume
core_image: 一块黄褐色的木料，刚削开就渗出清甜的香气
scene: 老街的香铺里，木匠正在打磨一块香木。The carpenter smoothed a block of sandalwood until the whole shop smelled sweet.
sceneCN: 这里 sandalwood 是「檀香木」（第 1 个义项：带有清甜香气的黄褐色木料）；句意：木匠把一块檀香木打磨光滑，直到整间铺子都弥漫着甜香。

pos.zh: 檀香（做定语，如檀香扇、檀香油）

derivatives.zh: 由本词的檀木义项简化而来，义为「檀木（山达木）」
由本词加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带檀香气味的」，属罕用书面说法
由本词加后缀 -er 构成，义为「采集或经营檀木的人」，极罕用

senses.title: The fragrant wood of the sandal tree
senses.definition: the yellowish-brown, sweetly scented wood of tropical trees of the genus Santalum, much used for carving and incense
senses.definitionCN: 檀香属热带树木所产的黄褐色、香气清甜的木材，常用来雕刻或焚香
senses.example: The little box was cut from a single piece of sandalwood.
senses.exampleCN: 这只小盒子是用一整块檀香木雕成的。
senses.why: The compound names the material itself: the tree called sandal plus wood, and the old custom of carving and burning this wood kept the basic sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是复合词：表示「檀木」的 sandal 加上 wood，古时雕刻与焚烧这种木料的习惯让这个最基本的义项一直保留下来。

senses.title: The sandal tree itself
senses.definition: an evergreen tree of the genus Santalum, native to southern Asia and other warm regions, whose heartwood yields the fragrance
senses.definitionCN: 檀香属常绿乔木，原产于南亚等地，心材散发香气
senses.example: Whole groves of sandalwood are protected by law in parts of India.
senses.exampleCN: 在印度部分地区，整片檀香林受法律保护。
senses.why: People do not only buy the wood; they know the crop and the crop needs a name, so the word shifts from material to the plant that yields it.
senses.whyCN: 人们不只购买木材，也种植、看护这种树，作物需要一个名字，词义便从「材料」转到「产材的树」。

senses.title: A sweet woody fragrance
senses.definition: the soft, warm, faintly sweet fragrance associated with this wood, used for perfumes and room scents
senses.definitionCN: 这种木料散发的柔和温甜香气，用于香水与室内香氛
senses.example: Her perfume has a warm base of sandalwood.
senses.exampleCN: 她的香水带着温暖的檀香基调。
senses.why: The smell stands for the wood that gives it; the sense is set off by the scent of, and it is used for perfumery and interiors.
senses.whyCN: 气味代表产生它的木料；这个义项由「某物的香气」这一搭配引出，用于香水与室内香氛。

senses.title: Fine carved articles
senses.definition: small objects such as boxes, fans, beads and statuettes made from this timber
senses.definitionCN: 用这种木料做成的小件，如盒子、扇骨、念珠与雕像
senses.example: The shop sells carved sandalwood fans that open with a soft click.
senses.exampleCN: 店里出售雕花檀木扇，打开时会发出轻轻的咔嗒声。
senses.why: This is the material as finished goods: the word acts like a classifier, so a fan or bead made of it is called a sandalwood fan or bead.
senses.whyCN: 这是「已做成器物」的材料：词在这里起定语作用，用这种木料制成的扇子或珠子就叫檀香扇、檀木珠。

senses.title: Incense and ritual use
senses.definition: incense made from this wood and burnt in temples, shrines and homes for worship, calming or meditation
senses.definitionCN: 用这种木料制成的香，在寺庙、神社与家中焚烧，用于祭拜、安神或冥想
senses.example: Monks burn sandalwood every morning before the first prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣每天早上在第一场祈愿前焚烧檀香。
senses.why: Because the wood burns slowly and smells gentle, it became the incense of worship; a commodity turns into a ritual act.
senses.whyCN: 这种木料燃烧缓慢、气味柔和，因而成了祭拜用的香；一种商品变成了一个仪式行为。

senses.title: As a modifier in product names
senses.definition: used before another noun to name products, often oils, soaps or foams, made with or scented by the wood
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，构成油、皂、膏等产品的名称，表示添加了这种木料或用其调香
senses.example: A bar of sandalwood soap sat beside the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 水槽边放着一块檀香皂。
senses.why: When the wood becomes an ingredient, its name moves in front of the product name and simply labels the flavour.
senses.whyCN: 当这种木料成为一种配料时，它的名字移到产品名前，只起到标注气味或成分的作用。

intro.en: Sandalwood joins an old word for the tree, which reached Europe through Sanskrit and Greek, with the plain English word wood.
intro.cn: sandalwood 把一个古老的树名与英语的 wood 组合起来；那个树名经由梵语与希腊语进入欧洲各语言。

items.en: Sanskrit candana names the fragrant sandal tree; the word is widely regarded as the origin of the later forms.
items.cn: 梵语 candana 指香檀树，一般认为它是后世各种拼写形式的源头。

items.en: Greek took the word as santalon, the name of a fragrant wood used in perfumes and the worship of the gods.
items.cn: 希腊语借入为 santalon，指用于香料与敬神的一种香木。

items.en: Medieval Latin records santalum, and Arabic forms such as sandal are usually invoked for the n sound, though the path is uncertain.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语记作 santalum；阿拉伯语中 sāndal 这样的形式常被认为带来了 n 音，但传播路径仍有争议。

items.en: Old French sandal reached England; the tree name appears in English from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 sandal 传入英国，树名在十四世纪见于英语。

items.en: Sandalwode is recorded, joining the tree name with wood and naming the timber rather than the tree.
items.cn: sandalwode 有记录，把树名与 wood 合在一处，指木料而不是树。

items.en: The spelling settles as sandalwood, and the word spreads into perfumery, carving, incense and cosmetics.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 sandalwood，这个词进入香水、雕刻、焚香与化妆品等领域。

note.en: The first group gathers words that look like or were shortened from the same tree name; the second gathers other aromatic woods and scents.
note.cn: 第一组收形近以及由同一树名简化而来的词；第二组收其他香木与香气词。

entries.definition: the sandal tree or its wood; it is not the same word as the footwear called sandal
entries.definitionCN: 檀木或檀香树，与表示凉鞋的 sandal 只是同形，词源不同。

entries.definition: having the scent of sandalwood; a rare literary adjective
entries.definitionCN: 带檀香气味的，属罕用书面形容词。

entries.definition: a tool or machine for smoothing wood with abrasive material; only spelling resembles sandalwood
entries.definitionCN: 打磨木材的工具或机器，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a person who gathers or deals in sandalwood; extremely rare
entries.definitionCN: 采集或经营檀木的人，极罕用。

entries.definition: the fragrant, reddish wood of the cedar, used in chests and pencils
entries.definitionCN: 雪松的红色香木，用于箱柜和铅笔。

entries.definition: a dark, highly prized fragrant wood used in incense and perfume in Asia
entries.definitionCN: 深色的珍贵香木，在亚洲用于制香和香水。

entries.definition: a hard tropical wood valued for furniture; it is durable but not aromatic
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬的热带木材，用于家具；耐用但无香味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real structure of the compound and the common products it names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用这一复合词的真实结构和它常常命名的产品。

normal.en: Sandalwood is literally sandal plus wood: the tree name joined to the word for timber.
normal.cn: sandalwood 字面上是 sandal 加 wood：树名与表示木材的词合在一起。

normal.en: The footwear sandal shares only the letters; its hair root has nothing to do with this wood.
normal.cn: 表示凉鞋的 sandal 只是拼写相同；它的词源与这种木料无关。

normal.en: Sandalwood oil is the concentrated version of the scent, so one drop carries the whole idea of the tree.
normal.cn: sandalwood oil 是气味的浓缩版，一滴油就承载了整棵树的意象。

normal.en: A sandalwood fan is a common carved product, which is why the word often appears before article names.
normal.cn: sandalwood fan 是常见的雕刻品，这也是这个词常出现在器物名前的原因。

normal.en: In temples the wood is burnt as incense, so the word also marks ritual calm.
normal.cn: 在寺庙里这种木料被烧成香，所以这个词还带上宗教与宁静的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a pale yellow block of wood, and a curl of shaving that smells sweet before it even reaches your nose.
abstract.cn: 想象一块浅黄色的木料，刨下来的木屑还没送到鼻尖就散出甜香。

abstract.en: Imagine a fan of thin sticks laid in a row, each one cut from the same fragrant tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一排薄薄的扇骨，每一根都取自同一棵香木。

abstract.en: Think of a thread of smoke rising from a small cone of incense in a quiet hall.
abstract.cn: 想象安静殿堂里，一小座香塔缓缓升起一线轻烟。

examples.en: He kept his letters in a carved sandalwood box.
examples.cn: 他把信件收在一只雕花檀木盒里。

examples.en: The room smelled of sandalwood and old paper.
examples.cn: 房间里飘着檀香与旧纸的气味。

examples.en: Sandalwood trees grow slowly, so their wood has become very expensive.
examples.cn: 檀香树生长缓慢，因此其木材变得非常昂贵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三打木头」——三斧子砍下一块香木，香味散开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 梵语 candana（香檀树）→ 希腊语 santalon → 中世纪拉丁语 santalum → 古法语 sandal → 英语 sandal + wood 合成 sandalwood「檀香木」。更早的梵语来源尚不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The six senses move along one line: from the fragrant timber, to the tree, to the scent, to carved objects, to ritual incense, to a modifier on product names.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项沿一条线展开：从香木料，到树木，到香气，到雕刻器物，到祭祀焚香，再到产品名前的定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a block of yellow-brown wood whose shavings give off a sweet scent.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黄褐色的木料，刨下的木屑散出清甜香气。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: the sweet-smelling timber is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 材质线：带香气的木料是最字面的义项。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the tree that grows the timber becomes a sense of its own.
branches.cn: 植物线：生长这种木料的树也独立成为一个义项。

branches.en: THE SCENT: the fragrance, and the long list of oils and soaps named after it.
branches.cn: 气味线：香气本身，以及以它命名的一系列油和皂。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: fans, boxes and beads show the timber turned into objects.
branches.cn: 工艺线：扇子、盒子与念珠体现木料变成器物。

branches.en: THE RITUAL: burnt in temples, the wood links sacred space to the slow-growing tree.
branches.cn: 仪式线：在寺庙中焚烧，这种木料把神圣空间与缓慢生长的树木连在一起。

intro.en: Sandalwood is a compound: an old tree name borrowed into English, plus the free morpheme wood.
intro.cn: sandalwood 是复合词：一个借入英语的古老树名，加上英语自有词素 wood。

latinIntro.en: The tree name is attested in Sanskrit, Greek and medieval Latin santalum, so only the deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个树名在梵语、希腊语与中世纪拉丁语 santalum 中都有记录，只有更早的来源不确定。

items.example: Candana is the earliest attested form of the tree name.
items.exampleCN: candana 是这一树名最早有记载的形式。

items.meaning: a fragrant wood used in perfume
items.example: Greek santalon passed the word into the Mediterranean trade.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 santalon 把这个词带进地中海贸易。

items.example: Santalum survives in the botanical genus name.
items.exampleCN: santalum 至今仍保留在植物属名中。

items.meaning: the sandal tree or its wood
items.example: Sandal is the bare tree name in English.
items.exampleCN: sandal 是英语中光秃秃的树名。

items.example: Wood names the material rather than the living plant.
items.exampleCN: wood 指木料，而不是活的植物。

items.example: The -d joins sandal and wood without carrying meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个 -d 把 sandal 和 wood 连在一起，本身没有含义。

items.meaning: used in names of timber trees
items.meaningCN: 用于木材树名，如红木、紫檀
items.example: The head -wood appears in rosewood and cedarwood too.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -wood 也出现在 rosewood 和 cedarwood 中。

items.meaningCN: 表示种类或集合的复数词尾
items.example: Sandalwoods can name several fragrant timber species.
items.exampleCN: sandalwoods 可以指几种香木树种。

items.example: The suffix forms the rare word sandalwooded.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成罕用词 sandalwooded。

definition_zh: 卫生的；清洁无菌的；卫生设施方面的；经期卫生用品的
definition_en: relating to health and cleanliness, or designed to keep conditions clean and free from disease
core_image: 一双手在水龙头下搓洗，脏东西顺水流走
scene: 厨房的后门通着垃圾堆，检查员走过来看了一眼水槽。The inspector found the kitchen was not sanitary enough to serve food.
sceneCN: 这里 sanitary 是「卫生的」（第 1 个义项：符合健康清洁标准的）；句意：检查员发现这间厨房不够卫生，不能供应食物。

collocations.zh: 卫生设施（厕所、盥洗设备）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「卫生设施；环境卫生」
由本词的词根加动词后缀构成，义为「消毒；使清洁」
由 sanitize 加 -er 构成，义为「消毒剂；洗手液」
同出拉丁词根 sanus「健康的」，义为「神志健全」，只是拼写相近

senses.title: Clean and free from germs
senses.definition: clean enough to protect health and free from dirt or substances that cause disease
senses.definitionCN: 清洁到足以保护健康，没有污物或致病物质
senses.example: Hospital kitchens must be kept strictly sanitary.
senses.exampleCN: 医院厨房必须保持严格卫生。
senses.why: Latin sanitas meant health, so sanitary first describes conditions that keep people healthy, and dirt is the visible enemy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sanitas 意为「健康」，所以 sanitary 首先描述能让人保持健康的状况，而污物就是看得见的敌人。

senses.title: Relating to public health
senses.definition: concerned with the protection of public health, especially through clean water, waste disposal and disease control
senses.definitionCN: 与保护公众健康有关的，尤指通过清洁水源、垃圾处理和疾病控制
senses.example: Sanitary reform in the Victorian era cut the death rate in cities.
senses.exampleCN: 维多利亚时代的公共卫生改革降低了城市死亡率。
senses.why: Once cleanliness becomes a duty of cities rather than of individuals, the word widens from a clean surface to whole systems of health.
senses.whyCN: 当清洁从个人的事变成城市的责任，这个词就从「表面干不干净」扩展到整套健康体系。

senses.title: Connected with toilets and washing
senses.definition: relating to plumbing fixtures, toilets and washing facilities, or used as a name for such equipment
senses.definitionCN: 与管道设备、厕所以及盥洗设施有关的，或直接用来命名这类器具
senses.example: The builders installed new sanitary ware in every flat.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方给每套公寓装了新的卫浴洁具。
senses.why: The place where hygiene is most obviously at stake is the bathroom, so sanitary attaches to the fixtures found there.
senses.whyCN: 最能体现卫生要求的地方是浴室和厕所，于是 sanitary 就粘在了那里常见的器具上。

senses.title: Used in feminine hygiene products
senses.definition: used in names for pads and similar products worn during menstruation
senses.definitionCN: 用于经期使用的护垫及类似产品的名称
senses.example: The clinic gives out free sanitary products to students.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所为学生们免费提供经期卫生用品。
senses.why: The adjective that marks cleanliness is borrowed politely for a product connected with bodily hygiene, which people once avoided naming directly.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示洁净的形容词被礼貌地借用来指涉身体卫生用品，因为这类东西过去不便直呼其名。

senses.title: Safe in the sense of waste disposal
senses.definition: describing a method of burying or handling waste in a way that prevents contamination
senses.definitionCN: 形容用掩埋或处理垃圾的方法，能避免污染
senses.example: Waste is buried in a sanitary landfill sealed with clay.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾被埋在用黏土封住的卫生填埋场里。
senses.why: Refuse is the opposite of hygiene, so a method that keeps refuse from leaking into soil is called sanitary.
senses.whyCN: 垃圾本身与卫生相反，所以能让垃圾不渗入土壤的处理方法就被称为「卫生的」。

intro.en: Sanitary is a nineteenth-century English adjective built on Latin sanitas, health, from sanus, healthy.
intro.cn: sanitary 是十九世纪英语造的形容词，建于拉丁语 sanitas（健康）之上，源于 sanus（健康的）。

items.en: The adjective sanus meant sound, healthy, not diseased, and it also underlies sanity and insane.
items.cn: 形容词 sanus 意为「健全的、健康的、无病的」，sanity 与 insane 也出自它。

items.en: The noun sanitas meant health, soundness of body and mind; Roman writers on medicine already linked it to diet and water.
items.cn: 名词 sanitas 意为「健康、身心健全」；罗马医学作家已把它与饮食和饮水联系起来。

items.en: The later phrase res sanitarias names matters of health, and this usage sits behind the English coinage.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁短语 res sanitarias 指「卫生事务」，这一用法为英语新造词提供了基础。

items.en: Sanitary appears in English in the first half of the nineteenth century during campaigns for clean water and drains.
items.cn: sanitary 于十九世纪上半年出现在英语中，当时正值争取清洁水源与下水道的运动。

items.en: The word spreads from public health to bathrooms, then to household products named after hygiene.
items.cn: 这个词从公共卫生扩展到浴室，再扩展到以卫生命名的家用产品。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin root of health; the second holds near synonyms that stress different parts of cleanliness.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「健康」拉丁词根构成的词；第二组收近义词，各自强调清洁的不同侧面。

entries.definition: the systems and facilities that remove human waste and keep places clean
entries.definitionCN: 清除人类排泄物、保持环境清洁的设施与体系。

entries.definition: to clean something so that germs are killed
entries.definitionCN: 消毒；使不含病菌。

entries.definition: the state of having a healthy mind
entries.definitionCN: 神志健全；心智健康。

entries.definition: seriously mentally ill; built on the same healthy root with a negative prefix
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常的，由同一「健康」词根加否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: clean and likely to prevent illness, with a strong medical flavour
entries.definitionCN: 清洁且能防病的，医学色彩更强。

entries.definition: completely free of living germs, used of medical equipment and instruments
entries.definitionCN: 完全无菌的，多用于医疗器械。

entries.definition: free from dirt; the everyday word, with no claim about health
entries.definitionCN: 干净的，是日常用语，不涉及健康含义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root of health and the fixed phrases the adjective appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用真实的拉丁「健康」词根，以及这个形容词固定的搭配。

normal.en: Sanus means healthy, so sanitary describes whatever keeps health safe.
normal.cn: sanus 意为健康，所以 sanitary 描述的是保住健康的那些条件。

normal.en: Sanitary conditions are the phrase to use when judging the cleanliness of a kitchen.
normal.cn: sanitary conditions 是评价厨房是否干净时的固定说法。

normal.en: Sanitary ware names the bowls and basins in a bathroom.
normal.cn: sanitary ware 指浴室里的盆与便器。

normal.en: Sanitary and sanity share a root but not a world: one is about bodies, the other about minds.
normal.cn: sanitary 与 sanity 同根但不同域：一个讲身体，一个讲心智。

normal.en: A sanitary landfill is named for stopping waste from leaking, not for making rubbish clean.
normal.cn: sanitary landfill 得名于阻止垃圾渗漏，而不是把垃圾变干净。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands under running water, soap bubbles carrying the dirt away down the drain.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手在水龙头下揉搓，肥皂泡把脏东西带进下水道。

abstract.en: From the drain, lift your eyes to a whole city of pipes and drains that carry sullage away from homes.
abstract.cn: 从下水口抬头，看到一个由管道和下水道构成的整座城市，把污水带离家家户户。

abstract.en: In the bathroom the same root reaches the white porcelain bowl: hygiene becomes an object you use every day.
abstract.cn: 在浴室里，同一词根触到洁白的瓷盆：卫生成了一个每天都会用到的物件。

examples.en: Many villages still lack basic sanitary facilities.
examples.cn: 许多村庄仍然缺乏基本的卫生设施。

examples.en: The factory was closed for the lack of sanitary conditions.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因缺乏卫生条件而被查封。

examples.en: Wash your hands and keep the work area sanitary before handling food.
examples.cn: 处理食物前请洗手，并保持操作区卫生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三拿水冲」——三遍水冲过才干净，就是卫生；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sanus（健康的）→ sanitas（健康）→ 晚期拉丁 res sanitarias（卫生事务）→ 英语 sanitary「卫生的」，与 sanity、insane 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From one root meaning health, sanitary widens into five senses: a clean surface, public health systems, bathroom fixtures, feminine products, and the safe handling of waste.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个意为「健康」的词根出发，sanitary 扩展出五个义项：干净的表面、公共卫生体系、卫浴器具、经期用品，以及垃圾的安全处理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands scrubbed under running water until the dirt is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手在水龙头下搓洗，直到脏东西被冲走。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a clean, germ-free place is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 表面线：干净无菌的场所是最日常的义项。

branches.en: THE CITY: public health turns the personal duty of cleanliness into an institution.
branches.cn: 城市线：公共卫生把个人的清洁义务变成一种制度。

branches.en: THE FIXTURES: bathrooms and their appliances inherit the word.
branches.cn: 器具线：浴室及其设备继承了这个词。

branches.en: THE BODY: products for monthly hygiene use the same polite adjective.
branches.cn: 身体线：经期卫生用品使用同一个委婉形容词。

branches.en: THE WASTE: keeping refuse and sullage contained extends the sense beyond the body.
branches.cn: 垃圾线：把垃圾和污水封住，使词义延伸到身体之外。

intro.en: Sanitary is Latin sanus plus the adjective suffix -ary; the family adds sanitize, sanitizer and sanitation.
intro.cn: sanitary 是拉丁语 sanus 加形容词后缀 -ary 构成；这个词族还包括 sanitize、sanitizer 与 sanitation。

latinIntro.en: Latin sanus and sanitas are both recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sanus 与 sanitas 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根不确定。

items.example: Sano is Latin for I heal.
items.exampleCN: sano 在拉丁语中表示「我医治」。

items.example: Sanitas is the direct base of sanitary.
items.exampleCN: sanitas 是 sanitary 的直接基础。

items.example: The suffix forms sanitary from health words.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把与健康相关的词构成 sanitary。

items.example: It forms sanitation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sanitation。

items.example: It forms sanitize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sanitize。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: It forms sanitizer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sanitizer。

items.example: The same root gives sanity.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还给出 sanity。

items.example: In plus sanus yields insane.
items.exampleCN: in 加 sanus 得到 insane。

items.example: It forms sanital, an obsolete form replaced by sanitary.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sanital，这是已被 sanitary 取代的旧形式。

definition_zh: 沙丁鱼；沙丁鱼罐头；（比喻）挤得像罐头里的沙丁鱼
definition_en: a small silvery fish of the herring family, often sold preserved in oil or tomato sauce in flat tins
core_image: 一只扁扁的铁皮罐头，里面银亮的鱼整整齐齐排成几层
scene: 鱼市场的摊位上，小银鱼堆成小山，摊主正把它们装罐。The stallholder packed hundreds of sardines into round tins for export.
sceneCN: 这里 sardine 是「沙丁鱼」（第 1 个义项：一种银色小鱼）；句意：摊主把几百条沙丁鱼装进圆铁罐准备出口。

pos.zh: （复数，比喻）拥挤的人群（见 packed like sardines）

collocations.zh: 挤得像沙丁鱼一样（拥挤不堪）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「像沙丁鱼的、带着鱼腥味的」，罕用
借自法语，与本词同源，指烤沙丁鱼等小鱼用的浅边小碟
由本词加指小后缀构成，指沙丁鱼属的近缘小鱼，科学术语

senses.title: A small silver fish
senses.definition: a small, silvery, oily fish of the herring family that swims in large shoals and is eaten fresh or preserved
senses.definitionCN: 鲱科的一种小型银色多脂鱼，成群游动，可鲜食也可加工保存
senses.example: Sardines feed on plankton and travel in shoals hundreds of metres wide.
senses.exampleCN: 沙丁鱼以浮游生物为食，鱼群宽度可达数百米。
senses.why: The word is first a fish name, probably handed down from the Mediterranean trade, and that concrete image of a tiny silver fish is the base of every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先是一个鱼名，很可能来自地中海贸易圈的口耳相传；这条银色小鱼的画面就是其他所有义项的源头。

senses.title: The preserved fish in tins
senses.definition: this fish cleaned, salted and packed in oil, brine or sauce inside a sealed flat tin, sold as a cheap staple food
senses.definitionCN: 把这种鱼清理、腌制后用油、盐水或酱汁封在扁平铁罐里的食品，是便宜的日常食物
senses.example: He put a tin of sardines and some bread on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他在桌上放了一罐沙丁鱼和一些面包。
senses.why: Because these fish spoil quickly, salting and canning became their main life, and the noun came to mean the packed product as well as the fish.
senses.whyCN: 这种鱼极易腐败，腌制与罐装成了它的主要形态；名词因此既指鱼，也指罐装产品。

senses.title: A packed crowd
senses.definition: in the phrase packed like sardines, describing people pressed tightly together in a small space
senses.definitionCN: 用于搭配 packed like sardines，形容人们在小空间里紧挨着挤成一团
senses.example: We were packed like sardines on the night train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在夜班火车上挤得像沙丁鱼一样。
senses.why: Small fish are laid in layers inside a flat tin, and the image of that tin is borrowed for a crowd with no room to turn.
senses.whyCN: 小鱼在扁平罐头里一层层叠放，罐头这个画面被借用过来说一群人挤得转不过身。

senses.title: A small and common thing
senses.definition: in phrases such as not a sardine, denoting a very small amount or a figure of no importance, used in jokes and informal talk
senses.definitionCN: 用于 not a sardine 之类的说法，表示极少的一点，或指不值一提的人物，见于玩笑与口语
senses.example: He did not earn a single sardine from that deal.
senses.exampleCN: 那笔买卖他一个子儿也没赚到。
senses.why: A fish this small packed by the hundred is the natural yardstick for something tiny, so the word moves from object to measure of triviality.
senses.whyCN: 这样小的鱼成百地装进罐头，自然成了衡量「小」的尺子；于是词义从实物转到了「微不足道」。

senses.title: A cheap and common food
senses.definition: the tinned fish taken as a symbol of plain, inexpensive, widely available food, and of modest means in general
senses.definitionCN: 把罐装的这种鱼当作朴素、便宜、随处可见的食物象征，泛指日子过得朴素
senses.example: Cans of sardines and a loaf of bread fed the household through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 几罐沙丁鱼和一条面包让一家人熬过冬天。
senses.why: The cheap tin sits on the bottom shelf of the shop, so the name comes to mark anything ordinary and low in price.
senses.whyCN: 便宜的罐头摆在商店最底层货架上，于是这个名字成了「普通、便宜」的标记。

intro.en: Sardine is a fish name from the Mediterranean, usually linked to the island of Sardinia, though the details are debated.
intro.cn: sardine 是来自地中海的鱼名，通常与撒丁岛相连，但具体来路仍有争论。

items.en: Ancient writers mention a small salted fish from around Sardinia; the exact Greek form behind the Latin name is not fully certain.
items.cn: 古代作家提到过产自撒丁岛附近的一种小咸鱼；拉丁名背后的确切希腊语形式尚不完全确定。

items.en: Latin sardina names a small fish, probably the pilchard, and the word is generally connected with Sardinia.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sardina 指一种小鱼，可能是沙丁鲱，一般认为与撒丁岛有关。

items.en: Old French sardine carries the word, and the general meaning is simply a small fish of the herring kind.
items.cn: 古法语 sardine 承袭此词，泛指鲱一类的小鱼。

items.en: The fish is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 这种鱼在十五世纪见于英语记载；确切首见时间不确定。

items.en: Industrial canning of the fish spread from Mediterranean ports in the nineteenth century, and the tin became part of the sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪工业化罐装从地中海港口扩散，铁皮罐头成为词义的一部分。

note.en: The look-alike group holds fish names that sound or look close; the near-meaning group holds other small fish and the crowded-crowd words.
note.cn: 形近组收发音或拼写相近的鱼名；近义组收其他小鱼，以及形容拥挤的词。

entries.definition: mocking and bitter in tone; it shares the first syllables only and comes from a different story
entries.definitionCN: 讥讽的、带苦味的，只是开头音节相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a striped gemstone made of onyx and chalcedony; only the spelling looks similar
entries.definitionCN: 一种带条纹的宝石，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: the Mediterranean island with which the fish name is traditionally connected
entries.definitionCN: 地中海上的岛屿，传统上被认为与这个鱼名有关。

entries.definition: a small flat dish in which sardines or similar fish are cooked, borrowed from French
entries.definitionCN: 法式小扁碟，用来烤沙丁鱼等小鱼，借自法语。

entries.definition: a heavy-set fish of the herring family, often the same species as the canned sardine
entries.definitionCN: 鲱科的一种体形较厚的鱼，常与罐头沙丁鱼是同一种。

entries.definition: a very small strong-flavoured fish, usually salted and put in tins or jars
entries.definitionCN: 一种极小的味重鱼，常腌制成罐头或瓶装。

entries.definition: a larger silvery fish of the same family, caught in cold northern seas
entries.definitionCN: 同科的银色大鱼，多见于寒冷的北方海域。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real name story and the fixed phrases the fish actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用鱼名真实的故事，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Sardinia is the island behind the name, so the fish and the place travel together.
normal.cn: sardine 得名于撒丁岛，鱼与地名一起流传。

normal.en: A tin of sardines is a fixed phrase: the container and the fish belong to each other.
normal.cn: a tin of sardines 是固定说法：罐头和鱼彼此离不开。

normal.en: Packed like sardines is the phrase for a crowd: layers of fish, no room to turn.
normal.cn: packed like sardines 指拥挤：鱼层叠着，连转身的余地都没有。

normal.en: Sardines are small, cheap and oily, which is why they became the food of hard times.
normal.cn: 沙丁鱼小、便宜、多脂，所以成了困难时期的食物。

normal.en: Sardonic looks close but carries no fish: it is about a bitter smile, not a tin.
normal.cn: sardonic 看起来相近却不含鱼：它讲的是苦笑的嘴，而不是铁皮罐。

abstract.en: Picture a flat silver tin opened with a curled key, and the rows of fish inside shining in oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只扁银罐用卷起的钥匙撬开，里面一排排鱼在油里发亮。

abstract.en: Now turn the tin on its side: if the fish could move, this is exactly the space a rush-hour carriage leaves a person.
abstract.cn: 再把罐头侧过来看：如果鱼会动，那正是高峰车厢一天留给人的空间。

abstract.en: Imagine a market table heaped with small silver fish, and a single shoal so wide that the sea darkens beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象鱼摊上堆满银色小鱼，再想海面下整片鱼群宽得让海水都暗下来。

examples.en: She opened a tin of sardines for supper.
examples.cn: 她晚饭时开了一罐沙丁鱼。

examples.en: The passengers were packed like sardines in the tiny bus.
examples.cn: 乘客们在狭小的巴士里挤得像沙丁鱼一样。

examples.en: Gulls follow the sardines as the shoal moves along the coast.
examples.cn: 鱼群沿岸移动时，海鸥跟在沙丁鱼后面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒丁丁」——撒丁岛一带的小鱼，一条条丁点大；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sardina（一种小鱼，一般认为与撒丁岛 Sardinia 有关）→ 古法语 sardine → 英语 sardine「沙丁鱼」；更早的希腊语形式不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Sardine starts as a fish name, then names the fish in its tin, then borrows the tin to describe a crowd, provisions and finally cheap everyday food.
sensesIntro.cn: sardine 先是鱼名，再指罐里的鱼，然后借铁皮罐头去形容拥挤的人群、随身携带的干粮，最后指廉价的日常食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat tin packed with layers of small silver fish.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只扁扁的罐头，里面层层排满银色小鱼。

branches.en: THE FISH: the small oily fish of the herring family is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 鱼线：鲱科的小型多脂鱼是最字面的义项。

branches.en: THE TIN: salting and canning gave the fish a second noun life.
branches.cn: 罐头线：腌制与罐装让这鱼有了第二个名词身份。

branches.en: THE CROWD: the packed tin is borrowed for people with no room to move.
branches.cn: 人群线：塞满的罐头被借来形容转不过身的人。

branches.en: THE POCKET: the tin that holds a whole meal stands for provisions carried on the day.
branches.cn: 口袋线：能装下一整顿饭的罐头，代表随身携带的当日口粮。

branches.en: THE SHELF: cheap tins on the bottom shelf make the word a measure of plain living.
branches.cn: 货架线：底层货架上的廉价罐头，让这个词成为朴素生活的标尺。

intro.en: Sardine is a borrowed noun without a live prefix or suffix; its family is thin, and the real building blocks are borrowing and compounding.
intro.cn: sardine 是借入的名词，本身没有活跃的前缀后缀；它的词族不大，真正的构词手段是借词与复合。

latinIntro.en: Latin sardina is recorded as a fish name and is generally tied to Sardinia, so only the oldest stage is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sardina 作为鱼名有记录，一般认为与撒丁岛有关，只有最古老的阶段不确定。

items.example: Latin sardina is the earliest firm form of the name.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 sardina 是这个名称最早确定的形态。

items.example: Sardinia is generally taken as the source of the fish name.
items.exampleCN: 撒丁岛一般被认为是这个鱼名的来源。

items.example: Sardines names a shoal or a number of tins.
items.exampleCN: sardines 指一群鱼或几罐鱼。

items.example: The rare word sardinish means like a sardine.
items.exampleCN: 罕用词 sardinish 意为「像沙丁鱼的」。

items.meaning: a container or a thing for
items.meaningCN: 表示容器或用于……的器具
items.example: Sardinière is the dish for cooking sardines.
items.exampleCN: sardinière 是烤沙丁鱼用的碟子。

items.example: A tin of sardines is the standard measure phrase.
items.exampleCN: a tin of sardines 是标准的量词搭配。

items.example: Packed like sardines borrows the image of a full tin.
items.exampleCN: packed like sardines 借用了满罐的画面。

items.example: Canned sardines is the common product name.
items.exampleCN: canned sardines 是常见的产品名。

items.example: Packed carries past participle form in the crowd idiom.
items.exampleCN: 在拥挤的习语里 packed 是过去分词形式。

definition_zh: 马尾藻；浮游在大洋表层的褐藻浮筏体；大量漂上海岸、堆积腐败的藻团
definition_en: a genus of brown seaweeds, and the floating masses of them that drift across the open ocean or wash ashore
core_image: 一片金褐色的小圆气囊托着细枝绿叶，在海面上组成了漂浮的草筏
scene: 渔民把捞上来的海藻摊在甲板上晾晒。Most of their catch that morning was sargassum pulled in with the nets.
sceneCN: 这里 sargassum 是「马尾藻（漂在海面上的藻类）」（第 1 个义项：马尾藻属的褐藻及其漂浮群落）；句意：那天早上他们捞上来的大部分东西，是随渔网一起拖上来的马尾藻。

pos.zh: 马尾藻浮筏；海水与海藻形成的大片漂浮植物群（常用于集合意义）

collocations.zh: 马尾藻海（被大量漂浮马尾藻覆盖的平静海域）
马尾藻类海藻（口语中把藻体直接称作「杂草」）
马尾藻暴发（温暖季节海中藻量陡然飙升）
马尾藻类海藻（强调是海藻而非其他水草）

forms.label: 学名复数（藻类拉丁名常用）

derivatives.zh: 由同一词源演变而来的专有地名用法，如马尾藻海，指藻体铺满水面的海域
词尾 -oid（相似的）加在 sargassum 之后的学术构词，形容形态类似马尾藻
罕见学术形容词，词尾 -aceous 表示「属于……的」，指属于马尾藻科

senses.title: Brown seaweed of the genus Sargassum
senses.definition: a group of brown seaweeds with small round air bladders, found in warm seas
senses.definitionCN: 一类生于暖海的褐藻，长有许多小圆气囊
senses.example: Sargassum grows quickly in warm, shallow water.
senses.exampleCN: 马尾藻在温暖浅水中长得很快。
senses.why: The name began as the Portuguese word for a kind of grape, and the rounded bladders were thought to look like little grapes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是葡萄牙语里一种葡萄的说法，因为马尾藻的圆气囊看上去像一串小葡萄，名字就这样转用到藻类身上。

senses.title: Floating mats of the weed
senses.titleCN: 马尾藻浮筏；海上漂浮藻团
senses.definition: the great floating patches of these seaweeds that drift on the open ocean
senses.definitionCN: 漂在开阔大洋表面、连成大片的海藻团
senses.example: Shrimp and young fish hide beneath the floating sargassum.
senses.exampleCN: 小虾和幼鱼躲在漂浮的马尾藻下面。
senses.why: Enough air bladders hold a whole colony at the surface, so the plant becomes a mass rather than a single stalk.
senses.whyCN: 气囊足够多，就能把整个群体托在水面，于是一株植物变成一片可漂移的「草筏」，义项由个体扩展到群体。

senses.title: A coastal nuisance and health hazard
senses.definition: huge amounts of the weed that wash onto beaches and rot, creating foul smells and costs
senses.definitionCN: 大量被冲上海滩并腐烂的海藻，造成恶臭与清理负担
senses.example: Nesting turtles had to crawl through piles of sargassum to reach the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 产卵的海龟不得不爬过成堆的马尾藻才能到海边。
senses.why: The same drifting mass that shelters fish can be pushed ashore by wind and currents, and once stranded it decays.
senses.whyCN: 庇护鱼群的漂浮藻团也会被风和海流推上岸，一旦搁浅便开始腐烂，于是这一义项带上了负面色彩。

senses.title: A source of fertilizer and food
senses.definition: the dried weed used as a plant food, or eaten in some coastal cuisines
senses.definitionCN: 晒干后用作植物肥料，或在部分沿海地区被当作食物
senses.example: Farmers spread dried sargassum over the vegetable beds.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把晒干的马尾藻铺在菜地里。
senses.why: Since the weed comes ashore in bulk, it can be collected and returned to the land as a cheap fertiliser, or used in cooking.
senses.whyCN: 海藻大量涌上岸，便于收集后送回陆地当廉价肥料，或在沿海料理中入菜，用途义项由此而生。

senses.title: A drifting nursery habitat
senses.definition: a habitat made of drifting weed that shelters young animals and small sea creatures
senses.definitionCN: 由漂移海藻构成的生境，为幼年动物和小型海洋生物提供藏身之处
senses.example: The sargassum provides shelter for more than a hundred species.
senses.exampleCN: 这片马尾藻为一百多种生物提供庇护。
senses.why: A mat of weed is a safe place in the open sea, so the plant also names the ecological role it plays as habitat.
senses.whyCN: 在开阔海面上，一片藻体就是一处安全地带，因此这个词也从「植物」延伸到它作为栖息地所起的作用。

intro.en: Sargassum is a modern scientific name built on an older word for a kind of grape, borrowed through Portuguese sailors naming the floating seaweed of the Atlantic.
intro.cn: sargassum 是近代科学命名，词干来自一个更早的「葡萄」类词，经由葡萄牙水手给大西洋漂浮海藻起的名字进入英语。

items.en: The plant name is compared with sargasso, a Portuguese word for a kind of grape, probably from a Latin grape name.
items.cn: 该植物名一般被认为与葡萄牙语词 sargasso（一种葡萄）相关，而后者可能源出某个拉丁语葡萄名称。

items.en: Portuguese sailors used sargaço for the drifting weed, perhaps because its round air bladders looked like grapes.
items.cn: 葡萄牙水手用 sargaço 称呼漂浮的海藻，可能是因为它的圆形气囊像葡萄。

items.en: Early English writers use sargasso for the weed and the sea it covers, giving the name Sargasso Sea.
items.cn: 早期英语用 sargasso 指这种海藻以及被它覆盖的海面，由此产生了 Sargasso Sea 这一海域名。

items.en: Nineteenth century naturalists latinise the name as Sargassum for the genus of brown algae.
items.cn: 十九世纪博物学家把名字拉丁化为 Sargassum，用作这类褐藻的属名。

items.en: Modern English uses sargassum for the genus and the floating weed, and for the mats that wash onto beaches.
items.cn: 现代英语用 sargassum 指该属海藻、漂浮的藻体，以及冲上海滩的藻团。

note.en: Sargassum sits next to the Sargasso Sea and older sargasso, and among the seaweeds and marine plants that share warm surface water.
note.cn: sargassum 与 Sargasso Sea、较早的 sargasso 相邻，也属于共享温暖表层海水的海藻与海洋植物词群。

entries.definition: older word for the floating weed, and for the calm sea covered by it
entries.definitionCN: 较早的词形，指漂浮海藻以及被它覆盖的平静海面

entries.definition: relating to or belonging to the family that contains sargassum
entries.definitionCN: 属于马尾藻科（含马尾藻属）的

entries.definition: shaped like or resembling sargassum
entries.definitionCN: 形态像马尾藻的

entries.definition: any large alga that grows in the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海藻的统称

entries.definition: a large brown seaweed, often growing in cold coastal water
entries.definitionCN: 海带类大型褐藻，多生于冷水海岸

entries.definition: simple plants that grow in water and have no true roots or leaves
entries.definitionCN: 藻类，水生、无真正根叶的简单植物

normalIntro.en: Sargassum is the weed of the Sargasso Sea: little air bladders holding a floating garden at the surface.
normalIntro.cn: sargassum 就是马尾藻海里的那种海藻：小气囊把一座漂浮花园托在水面上。

normal.en: Sargassum and Sargasso come from the same old word, linked to the sea covered with it.
normal.cn: sargassum 与 sargasso 来自同一个旧词，都与被它覆盖的海面相关。

normal.en: A sargassum bloom is a sudden surge in the amount of this weed in the sea.
normal.cn: sargassum bloom 指海中这种海藻数量突然激增。

normal.en: Round air bladders act like tiny floats, keeping the weed near the surface.
normal.cn: 圆形的气囊像小浮标，让海藻贴近水面。

normal.en: The Sargasso Sea is named for the weed, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 是先有这种海藻，才有了马尾藻海这个名字，而不是反过来。

normal.en: In biology, genus names such as Sargassum are printed in italics or with a capital letter.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，Sargassum 这类属名通常斜体书写或以大写开头。

abstract.en: Picture a grape-like cluster of floats bobbing on a still blue sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一串像葡萄的气囊在平静的蓝色海面上起伏。

abstract.en: Imagine a raft made of seaweed gliding slowly with the current while fish hide underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘用海藻编成的筏子随洋流缓缓滑行，鱼儿藏在下面。

abstract.en: Picture a beach carpeted with brown weed that rots and smells in the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海滩铺满褐色海藻，在阳光下腐烂发臭。

examples.en: Scientists are tracking a huge sargassum bloom across the Atlantic.
examples.cn: 科学家正在追踪大西洋上一场规模巨大的马尾藻暴发。

examples.en: The floating sargassum shelters juvenile fish and sea turtles.
examples.cn: 漂浮的马尾藻庇护着幼鱼与海龟。

examples.en: Hotels spend millions clearing sargassum from their beaches each summer.
examples.cn: 每家酒店每年夏天都要花几百万美元清理沙滩上的马尾藻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「洒嘎森」——水手往海面撒下一片嘎吱作响的海藻，长成会漂浮的小森林；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 经由葡萄牙语 sargaço（一种海藻；一般认为与表示「葡萄」的旧词同源，追至拉丁语葡萄类名称）→ 英语 sargasso（漂浮海藻；马尾藻海）→ 十九世纪拉丁化为 Sargassum（马尾藻属）。

sensesIntro.en: From the single brown seaweed, sargassum widens to the floating mats it forms, to the rotting weed on beaches, to its uses as fertiliser and food, and to its role as a drifting nursery.
sensesIntro.cn: sargassum 从单株褐藻开始，扩展为它形成的漂浮藻团，再到冲上海滩的腐败藻体，又衍生出肥料与食材的用途义，最后成为漂浮育幼场的生境义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sunlit raft of air floats bearing feathery brown weed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一簇气囊托着羽状褐藻，在阳光下的海面漂成一只筏子。

branches.en: The genus itself is the botanical sense.
branches.cn: 属名所指的植物本身是植物学义项。

branches.en: The mat is both a physical mass and a habitat.
branches.cn: 浮筏既是物理上的藻团，也是生物栖息地。

branches.en: Stranded weed turns into a coastal nuisance.
branches.cn: 搁浅的藻体变成沿海的麻烦。

branches.en: A bulk material that can be gathered has practical uses.
branches.cn: 可以大量收集的材料便有了实际用途。

branches.en: The same drifting mass that shelters life can also spoil a beach.
branches.cn: 同一片漂浮藻团既庇护生命，也可能毁掉一片海滩。

intro.en: Sargassum is a single borrowed stem with few English affixes, so the word family is small and mostly technical.
intro.cn: sargassum 基本是一个借来的词干，英语词缀很少，词族也小，多为学术用法。

latinIntro.en: The word was latinised for scientific use: the stem sargass- plus the Latin neuter ending -um marks it as a genus name.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词为科学用途做了拉丁化处理：词干 sargass- 加上拉丁语中性词尾 -um，成为属名。

items.meaning: the seaweed named after a kind of grape
items.meaningCN: 以「葡萄」命名的海藻词干
items.example: The stem sargass- carries the whole name.
items.exampleCN: 词干 sargass- 承载了整个名称的含义。

items.meaningCN: 标记拉丁语中性名词的词尾
items.example: The ending -um makes Sargassum a genus name.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -um 使 Sargassum 成为属名。

items.meaning: the plural of Latin neuter nouns in -um
items.meaningCN: 拉丁语中性名词 -um 的复数词尾
items.example: The plural ending gives sargassa.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数词尾构成 sargassa。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms sargassoid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 构成 sargassoid。

items.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of
items.example: The suffix -aceous forms sargassaceous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -aceous 构成 sargassaceous。

items.meaning: a wild plant, used loosely for floating sea plants
items.meaningCN: 野生植物，口语中也泛指漂浮的海生植物
items.example: The compound sargassum weed names the drifting plant.
items.exampleCN: sargassum weed 这一复合说法指漂浮的藻体。

items.meaning: a sudden rapid growth of plants or algae
items.example: The phrase sargassum bloom describes a sudden surge.
items.exampleCN: sargassum bloom 描述数量骤然激增。

items.meaning: the older form of the same name
items.example: Sargasso survives in the sea name.
items.exampleCN: Sargasso 保留在海域名称中。

latinEntries.meaning: seaweed, and a kind of grape
latinEntries.meaningCN: 海藻；亦指一种葡萄（葡萄牙语）

definition_zh: 使吃饱；使充分满足；使过量、腻味
definition_en: to satisfy someone fully, especially with food, so that they want no more
core_image: 餐桌上摆满菜肴，吃到最后一个客人也放下筷子，再也吃不下了
scene: 晚宴的菜越上越多，客人们渐渐吃不下了。The endless dishes finally satiated even the hungriest guests.
sceneCN: 这里 satiate 是「使吃饱」（第 1 个义项：用食物使人充分饱足）；句意：一道道不停端上的菜，终于让最饿的客人也吃不下了。

pos.zh: 使充分满足（欲望、需求等）
（书面）饱足的；满足的；（古）已获充分满足的

collocations.zh: 完全满足的；吃得非常饱的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语词干 sati- 加名词后缀 -ety，义为「饱足；满足」
与 satiate 同出拉丁语 satis（足够），经法语进入英语，义为「使满足；符合要求」
同一词根 satur- 加 -ation 构成的名词，义为「饱和；浸透」
否定前缀 in- 加 satiable，义为「不知足的；无法满足的」

senses.title: To fill someone with food
senses.definition: to give someone so much food that they feel completely full
senses.definitionCN: 给某人吃足够多的食物，使之完全饱腹
senses.example: A single bowl of noodles did not satiate the hungry child.
senses.exampleCN: 一碗面并不能让这个饥饿的孩子吃饱。
senses.why: The Latin source satis means enough, so to satiate is to bring someone up to the point of enough.
senses.whyCN: 词源中的拉丁语 satis 意为「足够」，因此 satiate 就是把人使到「足够」那个点，落在食物上便是吃饱。

senses.title: To satisfy a desire completely
senses.definition: to satisfy a desire, need, or interest so fully that nothing more is wanted
senses.definitionCN: 充分满足欲望、需求或兴趣，直到不再渴求
senses.example: One long holiday satiated her longing for travel.
senses.exampleCN: 一次长假满足了她对旅行的渴望。
senses.why: The same image of reaching enough extends from food to any craving, so appetite and desire alike can be satiated.
senses.whyCN: 「达到足够」的画面从食物延伸到任何渴求，于是食欲、欲望、兴趣都可以被这个动词填满。

senses.title: To give more than enough
senses.definition: to provide so much of something that it becomes tedious or unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 提供得太多，以致令人厌烦或不再想要
senses.example: Constant praise can satiate a reader and dull the taste for detail.
senses.exampleCN: 接连不断的夸赞会让读者腻味，冲淡对细节的品尝能力。
senses.why: Enough pushed past its limit becomes too much, so the verb also carries a note of surfeit and boredom.
senses.whyCN: 「足够」一旦越过界线就变成「过多」，所以这个词也带上「过量、吃腻」的意味。

senses.title: Satisfied with a market
senses.definition: to fill demand so completely that no further supply is needed
senses.definitionCN: 把需求填满，以致不再需要更多供应
senses.example: Cheap imports quickly satiated the demand for basic tools.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口货很快满足了人们对基础工具的需求。
senses.why: A market, like a stomach, has a capacity, so filling it fully is a natural commercial extension.
senses.whyCN: 市场和胃一样有容量，把它填满就是自然的商业引申。

senses.title: Sated, in literary use
senses.definition: full, satisfied, and often weary, used as a rare adjective
senses.definitionCN: 饱满、满足，常常带倦意，是稀见的形容词用法
senses.example: Satiate guests drifted away from the long banquet table.
senses.exampleCN: 酒足饭饱的客人们一个个离开了长长的宴会桌。
senses.why: The past participle grew into a separate adjective, keeping the image of someone who has had enough.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词后来独立成形容词，保留「已经吃够、够数」的画面。

intro.en: Satiate comes from the Latin verb satiare, to fill or satisfy, which rests on satis, enough.
intro.cn: satiate 来自拉丁语动词 satiare（填满、使满足），其核心为 satis（足够）。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually given as meaning enough or sufficient lies behind satis.
items.cn: 一般认为 satis 背后有一个重构词根，表示「足够」。

items.en: Satis means enough, and the verb satiare means to fill, satisfy, or glut.
items.cn: satis 意为「足够」，动词 satiare 意为「填满、使满足、使腻」。

items.en: The participle satiatus, filled or glutted, is used in writers of the late empire.
items.cn: 分词 satiatus（已填满、已腻）见于帝国晚期的作家。

items.en: Related forms include satietas, fullness, and satur, full, which feed other English words.
items.cn: 相关形式还有 satietas（饱满）与 satur（满的），它们也供给了其他英语词。

items.en: English borrows satiate directly from Latin as a verb meaning to fill to the full.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪直接从拉丁语借入 satiate，作动词表示「填到满」。

items.en: The verb takes on desire, markets, and audiences, and the participle becomes an adjective.
items.cn: 此后它扩展到欲望、市场与读者，分词也固定为形容词。

note.en: Satiate shares the Latin root for enough with satisfy, satiety, and saturation, and it sits close to words of fullness and glutting.
note.cn: satiate 与 satisfy、satiety、saturation 共享拉丁语「足够」词根，并与表示「饱足、腻味」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being full or having enough
entries.definitionCN: 饱足；饱腻的状态

entries.definition: completely full or fully satisfied
entries.definitionCN: 已吃饱的；已充分满足的

entries.definition: the state of being filled completely
entries.definitionCN: 饱和；浸透

entries.definition: to meet a need or wish
entries.definitionCN: 使满足；满足（需求）

entries.definition: to supply so much that there is too much
entries.definitionCN: 使供应过剩；使过饱

entries.definition: to give too much of something, especially food
entries.definitionCN: 使过量（尤指食物）；使腻

normalIntro.en: Satiate is built on the Latin idea of enough: to reach the line of enough is to be full.
normalIntro.cn: satiate 建立在对拉丁语「足够」的理解上：到达「足够」那条线就是饱了。

normal.en: The noun satiety is the state of being full; the verb satiate is what brings that state.
normal.cn: 名词 satiety 是「饱足状态」，动词 satiate 则是造成这种状态的动作。

normal.en: To satiate your appetite is the commonest collocation.
normal.cn: satiate your appetite（满足食欲）是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Add in- and satiable gives insatiable, unable to be satisfied.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 与 satiable 便得到 insatiable，义为「无法满足的」。

normal.en: The -ate ending often signals a verb, as in satiate, animate, and cultivate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 常标示动词，如 satiate、animate、cultivate。

normal.en: The participial adjective fully satiated describes someone who has had enough.
normal.cn: 分词形容词 fully satiated 形容一个人已经吃够、喝够了。

abstract.en: Picture a table heaped with dishes until no one can lift a chopstick.
abstract.cn: 想象一张堆满菜的桌子，直到没有人能再抬起筷子。

abstract.en: Imagine a thirst that a whole bottle cannot quench.
abstract.cn: 想象一种连一整瓶水也解不了的渴。

abstract.en: Think of a filling fire being built up until it needs no more wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆火被填到极致，再也塞不进任何柴。

examples.en: Two helpings of dumplings satiated the tired workers.
examples.cn: 两盘饺子让疲惫的工人们吃饱了。

examples.en: No amount of entertainment could satiate his curiosity about the stars.
examples.cn: 再多的消遣也满足不了他对星辰的好奇。

examples.en: They satiated the demand for cheap housing within a single year.
examples.cn: 他们在一年之内就满足了人们对廉价住房的需求。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞他 it」——把东西一直往他那边塞，塞到他吃下 it 就饱了；这只是读音联想，并非来自词源。

root: 重构词根「足够」→ 拉丁语 satis（足够）→ satiare（使填满、使满足）→ 分词 satiatus → 英语动词 satiate；同源词族含 satiety、satisfy、saturation。

sensesIntro.en: Satiate starts from filling a stomach to the point of enough, then fills any desire in the same way, passes into the excess of glutting, extends to markets, and settles into a rare adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: satiate 始于把肚子填到「足够」，再以同样方式填满任何欲望，接着滑向过量的腻味，延伸到市场需求，最后固定为一个稀见的形容词。
