core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table whose dishes finally leave every guest full.
core.cn: 核心意象：满桌菜肴终于把每位客人都填饱。

branches.en: Food is the original object of the verb.
branches.cn: 食物是这个词最早的对象。

branches.en: Desire and demand are filled the same way.
branches.cn: 欲望与需求以同样的方式被填满。

branches.en: Too much turns fullness into weariness.
branches.cn: 给予过多，把饱足变成了厌倦。

branches.en: The participle becomes a literary adjective.
branches.cn: 分词独立为书面形容词。

branches.en: A person who has been filled is described by the same idea.
branches.cn: 被填满的人由同一个概念来描述。

intro.en: Satiate is a Latin borrowing; its small family grows through -ety, -able, in-, and the related stems satur- and satisf-.
intro.cn: satiate 是拉丁语借词，其小词族通过 -ety、-able、否定前缀 in- 以及 satur-、satisf- 等相关词干扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is satis, enough, from which satiare, satietas, and satur all develop.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语核心是 satis（足够），satiare、satietas 与 satur 都由它派生。

items.example: Satis gives the sense of reaching the line of enough.
items.exampleCN: satis 给出「到达足够那条线」的含义。

items.example: Satiare is the direct source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: satiare 是该动词的直接来源。

items.meaning: marks a verb or a verb-derived adjective
items.meaningCN: 标示动词或由动词而来的形容词
items.example: The ending -ate marks satiate as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 标示 satiate 是动词。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ety forms satiety.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ety 构成 satiety。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms satiated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 satiated。

items.example: The prefix in- builds insatiable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 insatiable。

items.example: The suffix -able forms satiable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 satiable。

items.example: The stem satur- gives saturation.
items.exampleCN: 词干 satur- 构成 saturation。

items.example: The stem satisf- gives satisfy.
items.exampleCN: 词干 satisf- 构成 satisfy。

derivatives.zh: 饱足；满足
不知足的；无法满足的
吃饱的；满足的

definition_zh: 缎木（产于斯里兰卡与印度的一种黄褐色硬木，可制高档家具）；产缎木的常绿树；缎木色
definition_en: a hard, yellowish, satiny wood from a tropical tree used for fine furniture, or the tree that yields it
core_image: 一块抛光后的浅金色木板，表面像缎子一样泛着丝滑柔光
scene: 老师傅用一块缎木修复旧柜子的抽屉面板。The craftsman chose satinwood for the drawer fronts because it polishes like silk.
sceneCN: 这里 satinwood 是「缎木（木料）」（第 1 个义项：用作高档家具的黄褐色硬木）；句意：这位工匠为抽屉面板选了缎木，因为它打磨后像丝绸一样光亮。

pos.zh: 缎木树（产此木材的常绿乔木）
（定语用法）缎木做的；缎木色的

collocations.zh: 缎木色的表面处理；缎面般的光泽
实心缎木（整块木材，非贴皮）

forms.label: 东印度缎木（植物学与贸易名）
西印度缎木（木材贸易名）

derivatives.zh: satinwood 的前半部分，指光滑如缎的丝织物，也用来比喻打磨后光亮的表面
satinwood 与 tree 组成的短语，明确指产这种木材的树种（对应第 2 个义项）
satin 加指小后缀 -et，指仿缎的棉毛织物，与 satinwood 同享「缎面」喻义
satin 的另一种指小构词，义同 satinet，指仿缎织物

senses.title: The polished hardwood itself
senses.definition: a hard, pale golden wood with a smooth, glossy grain, prized for fine furniture
senses.definitionCN: 一种浅金黄色、纹理平滑光亮的硬木，常用作高档家具
senses.example: The drawer front was cut from a single piece of satinwood.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉面板是用一整块缎木做的。
senses.why: The word joins satin and wood, because once sanded the grain glows like a length of silk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 satin（缎子）与 wood（木材）合成，因为打磨后它的纹理就像一段绸缎那样发亮，所以指这种木料。

senses.title: The tree that yields the wood
senses.definition: a tall evergreen tree of warm regions whose timber is this satiny wood
senses.definitionCN: 生长于温暖地区的常绿乔木，其木材即上述缎木
senses.example: Satinwood trees grow slowly in the forests of Sri Lanka.
senses.exampleCN: 缎木树在斯里兰卡的林地里生长缓慢。
senses.why: In English, names of materials routinely stand for the plant that produces them, so the tree inherits the wood name.
senses.whyCN: 英语里材料名常直接指产出它的植物，于是这种树也继承了木料的名称。

senses.title: A colour name
senses.definition: a pale yellowish brown shade named after the timber
senses.definitionCN: 以这种木材命名的浅黄褐色
senses.example: The ceiling was painted in a soft satinwood tone.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板被刷成柔和的缎木色。
senses.why: Colours are often borrowed from prized materials, and the pale golden wood offered a ready shade name.
senses.whyCN: 颜色名常借用贵重材料，这种浅金色的木材自然成了现成的色名。

senses.title: A mark of formal design
senses.definition: the wood as a feature of neo-classical and colonial furniture, prized for inlay and veneer
senses.definitionCN: 作为新古典与殖民地家具特征的木材，常用于镶嵌与贴皮
senses.example: Satinwood inlaid with darker woods became a signature of the era.
senses.exampleCN: 用深色木材镶嵌的缎木成了那个时代的标志。
senses.why: Because the wood is pale and hard, craftsmen used it as a glowing ground for inlaid patterns, so the material names a style as well.
senses.whyCN: 这种木材色浅而坚硬，工匠常用它作镶嵌图案的明亮底色，于是材料名也成了一种风格标签。

senses.title: A protected ornamental timber
senses.definition: a slow-growing tropical timber whose selling is restricted or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 生长缓慢的热带木材，其买卖受到限制或管制
senses.example: Dealers must certify that the satinwood was legally harvested.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商必须证明这些缎木是合法采伐的。
senses.why: Slow growth and heavy demand pushed the timber into trade limits, so the word also appears in conservation and customs talk.
senses.whyCN: 生长缓慢而需求旺盛，这种木材被纳入贸易限制，于是这个词也出现在保护与海关语境中。

intro.en: Satinwood is an English compound of two ordinary words, satin and wood, coined to describe a timber that shines like silk.
intro.cn: satinwood 是英语中由 satin 与 wood 两个普通词合成的复合词，用来形容一种光泽如绸缎的木材。

items.en: Satin reached Europe as a name for a smooth silk, brought along trade routes from the east.
items.cn: satin 作为光滑丝绸的名称，沿贸易路线从东方传入欧洲。

items.en: The silk name passes into French as satin, and then into Middle English.
items.cn: 这一丝绸名以 satin 进入法语，再进入中古英语。

items.en: English joiners borrow the shine of satin to name tropical timber, giving satinwood.
items.cn: 英国细木匠借用缎子的光泽为热带木材命名，构成 satinwood。

items.en: Satinwood veneer becomes fashionable in neo-classical furniture in Britain.
items.cn: 十八世纪后期，缎木贴皮在英国新古典家具中风行。

items.en: Botanists apply the trade word to several unrelated trees sold under the name.
items.cn: 十九世纪，植物学家把这一商贸词用于多种名称相同却并不同源的树种。

items.en: Modern usage spans timber, tree, colour, and conservation restrictions.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖木料、树种、颜色与保护限制几个层面。

note.en: Satinwood is built from satin and wood, and it stands beside other named furniture timbers and silk-bright materials.
note.cn: satinwood 由 satin 与 wood 合成，常与其它以材质命名的家具木材及「缎面般光亮」的材料词并列。

entries.definition: a smooth, glossy fabric
entries.definitionCN: 缎子，光滑闪光的丝织物

entries.definition: a cotton cloth made to imitate satin
entries.definitionCN: 仿缎的棉织物

entries.definition: a lightweight imitation satin
entries.definitionCN: 轻薄的仿缎织物

entries.definition: a reddish-brown hardwood used for furniture
entries.definitionCN: 桃花心木，红褐色硬木，常做家具

entries.definition: a hard, durable tropical wood
entries.definitionCN: 柚木，坚固耐用的热带木材

entries.definition: a very dark, dense wood, used for inlay
entries.definitionCN: 黑檀，极深色的致密木材，常用于镶嵌

normalIntro.en: Satinwood says what it is: wood with the shine of satin, so the two halves tell the whole story.
normalIntro.cn: satinwood 名字即定义：有缎子光泽的木头，两个词根就把意思讲完了。

normal.en: Satinwood is a compound of satin and wood, and the stress falls on the first part.
normal.cn: satinwood 是 satin 与 wood 的复合词，重音落在前半部分。

normal.en: A satinwood cabinet or veneer is a usual collocation in descriptions of furniture.
normal.cn: satinwood cabinet 与 satinwood veneer 是描述家具时的常见搭配。

normal.en: Trade names such as East Indian satinwood and West Indian satinwood mark different trees sold under one label.
normal.cn: East Indian satinwood 与 West Indian satinwood 等贸易名，标示着冠以同一名称的不同树种。

normal.en: Compare mahogany and teak: the same pattern of wood name built from colour or shine.
normal.cn: 对比 mahogany 与 teak：同样是按颜色或光泽命名的木材。

normal.en: Satinwood often pairs with inlay, veneer, and polishing in craft writing.
normal.cn: 在工艺文字里，satinwood 常与镶嵌、贴皮、打磨等词同现。

abstract.en: Picture a pale golden board catching the light like a folded silk scarf.
abstract.cn: 想象一块浅金色木板，反光处像一条叠好的丝巾。

abstract.en: Imagine a cabinet maker turning a glossy plank so its grain flashes along the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象细木匠转动一块光亮的木板，木纹在边上闪成一道光。

abstract.en: Think of a pale timber line inlaid with darker bands like a ribbon on cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象浅色木料被镶上深色木条，像布上系的丝带。

examples.en: The antique writing desk is faced with satinwood and inlaid with ebony.
examples.cn: 这张古董写字桌面贴着缎木，并镶嵌着黑檀。

examples.en: Restorers had to match the new satinwood to the old grain.
examples.cn: 修复师得让新缎木与旧木纹相配。

examples.en: Because the satinwood trees grow so slowly, the timber is strictly controlled.
examples.cn: 由于缎木树长得极慢，这种木材受到严格管制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缎子木」——把 satin（缎子）和 wood（木头）合在一起，像缎子一样发亮的木头就是缎木；这只是拆词联想，并非完整词源。

root: satin（缎子，源自东方的丝绸名，经法语 satin 进入中古英语）+ wood（木头）→ 英语复合词 satinwood，取「打磨后光泽似缎」之意。

sensesIntro.en: Satinwood begins as the name of a glossy timber, extends to the tree that supplies it, to a colour borrowed from it, to its role in inlaid design, and finally to its status as a restricted trade wood.
sensesIntro.cn: satinwood 最初指一种光亮的木料，继而扩展到产出它的树木、借其命名的颜色，再成为镶嵌设计中的标志材料，最后带上受管制贸易用材的身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polished pale board whose grain shines like silk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块抛光的浅色木板，木纹亮得像绸缎。

branches.en: The material sense is the starting point.
branches.cn: 材料义是这个词的起点。

branches.en: The material names the plant that produces it.
branches.cn: 材料名转而指产出它的植物。

branches.en: The wood becomes a colour reference.
branches.cn: 木材成为颜色参照。

branches.en: The material marks a period design style.
branches.cn: 这种材料成为某个时期风格的标志。

branches.en: A slow-growing tree turns a luxury wood into a guarded commodity.
branches.cn: 生长缓慢的树木，把奢侈木料变成受看管的大宗商品。

intro.en: Satinwood is a native English compound; its parts are satin, itself a borrowing, and the common noun wood.
intro.cn: satinwood 是英语本土复合词，由借词 satin 与常用名词 wood 两部分构成。

latinIntro.en: Satin is not of Latin origin; it came west along the silk trade, so the Latin element here is limited to the French form satin.
latinIntro.cn: satin 并非拉丁语来源，而是沿丝绸贸易西传；这里所谓「拉丁」成分仅指法语形式 satin。

items.example: Satin supplies the shine in satinwood.
items.exampleCN: satin 提供 satinwood 中「光亮」的意象。

items.meaning: the hard material of a tree
items.example: Wood fixes the material sense of the compound.
items.exampleCN: wood 锁定这个复合词的材料义。

items.meaning: used in names of timbers and timber trees
items.meaningCN: 构成木材或树种名称的构词成分
items.example: The combining form -wood also builds rosewood.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -wood 也构成 rosewood。

items.meaning: used to name the plant that supplies a timber
items.meaningCN: 用于指产某种木材的树木
items.example: The combining form -tree gives satinwood tree.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -tree 构成 satinwood tree。

items.example: The suffix -et forms satinet from satin.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -et 由 satin 构成 satinet。

items.example: The suffix -ette forms satinette.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ette 构成 satinette。

items.meaning: of the East Indies or Indian subcontinent
items.meaningCN: 东印度或印度次大陆的
items.example: The modifier East Indian names one trade grade.
items.exampleCN: 修饰语 East Indian 标出其中一个贸易等级。

items.example: The modifier West Indian marks a different timber.
items.exampleCN: 修饰语 West Indian 标示另一种木材。

items.meaning: a thin layer of fine wood
items.example: Satinwood veneer covers cheaper timber.
items.exampleCN: 缎木贴皮覆盖在较便宜的木材上。

items.meaning: a design set into a surface
items.example: Satinwood often carries inlays of darker wood.
items.exampleCN: 缎木常嵌有更深的木料图案。

definition_zh: 使浸透；使饱和；充满；使（颜色）饱和；使（信号等）饱和
definition_en: to soak something completely, or to fill it so fully that no more can be added
core_image: 海绵吸满水，捏一下都滴不出空隙
scene: 南方的小雨下了整夜，土坡上的泥土吸足了水，踩上去直冒泡。Rain filled every gap in the soil, and the ground sat saturated. Pools formed. Each step sprayed mud.
sceneCN: 这里 saturate 是「使浸透」（第 1 个义项：液体把某物里里外外填满）；句意：雨水灌满了土壤的空隙，地面一直吸饱了水，积起水洼，每一步都溅起泥浆。

pos.zh: 使浸透；使饱和；充满；使（颜色或信号）饱和
饱和的（多见于 chemistry 等学科语境）

derivatives.zh: 由 saturate 加 -ion 构成，义为「饱和；浸透」
过去分词用作形容词，义为「饱和的；浸透的」
由前缀 super- 加 saturate 构成，义为「使过饱和」

senses.title: To soak something completely
senses.definition: to make something completely wet so that it holds as much liquid as it can
senses.definitionCN: 使某物彻底湿透，能吸多少液体就吸多少
senses.example: Heavy rain saturated the fields overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨一夜之间把田地浇透了。
senses.why: Latin saturare means to fill completely, and the first thing a full sponge shows is liquid that has soaked in everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 saturare 意为「填满」，而一个装满的海绵最直观地显示了液体浸透各处，所以「浸透」是它最具体的第一义。

senses.title: To fill to the point of no more
senses.definition: to fill a space, supply, or market so fully that nothing more can be added
senses.definitionCN: 把空间、供应或市场填得满满的，再也加不进新的东西
senses.example: New shops have saturated the local market.
senses.exampleCN: 新开的商店让本地市场饱和了。
senses.why: Once the sponge can hold nothing more, the same picture turns into a limit, so saturate gains the sense of a supply that has no room left.
senses.whyCN: 海绵吸不下更多水时，同一个画面就变成了「上限」，于是 saturate 引申出「供应多到再没有余量」的饱和义。

senses.title: To spread through every part
senses.definition: to be present in every part of a place, medium, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 存在于某地、某介质或某种处境的每个角落
senses.example: The air was saturated with soot and steam.
senses.exampleCN: 空气里弥漫着煤灰和水汽。
senses.why: Soaking means the liquid reaches every fibre, so a smell, sound, or feeling that reaches every corner can also saturate a place.
senses.whyCN: 浸透就是液体到达每一根纤维，因此一种气味、声音或情绪渗透到每个角落时，也可以用 saturate 来表达。

senses.title: To hold an excess for special use
senses.definition: to force something to hold or display more energy, data, or intensity than is usual
senses.definitionCN: 迫使某物承载或显示超出通常水平的能量、数据或强度
senses.example: The signal saturated the receiver circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 信号使接收电路饱和了。
senses.why: Technical uses push the full-sponge idea to its limit, where a channel holds as much signal as it can before the extra is lost.
senses.whyCN: 技术领域的用法把「吸满」推到极端：通道承载了能装下的全部信号，多出的部分就会溢出丢失。

senses.title: To make a colour deep and intense
senses.definition: to make a colour rich, pure, and intense rather than pale or greyish
senses.definitionCN: 使某颜色浓郁、纯粹而不发白或发灰
senses.example: Photo editing tools can saturate the sky a little.
senses.exampleCN: 修图工具可以把天空的颜色调饱和一点。
senses.why: A fully soaked cloth shows its dye at its strongest, so an image or pigment with no white left in it is called saturated.
senses.whyCN: 布料吸透染料后颜色最浓，因此图像或颜料里不再掺白、颜色达到最浓时，就说它是饱和的。

intro.en: Saturate comes from Latin saturare, to fill or sate, from satur, full or sated, the same family that gave English satire.
intro.cn: saturate 来自拉丁语 saturare（填满、使饱足），源于 satur（饱的、满满的），与英语 satire 同属一族。

items.en: Satur describes something full or sated.
items.cn: satur 形容某物满满的、饱足的。

items.en: Saturare means to fill up or make full.
items.cn: saturare 意为装满、填满。

items.en: Saturatus is the past participle and supplies the adjective saturated.
items.cn: saturatus 是过去分词，为形容词 saturated 提供依据。

items.en: The word enters English in chemistry as a verb about filling a solution.
items.cn: 该词在化学领域以动词身份进入英语，指把溶液填满。

items.en: Modern English adds markets, media signals, and colour saturation.
items.cn: 现代英语又扩展出市场饱和、信号饱和与颜色饱和等用法。

note.en: Saturate is the verb of being full: it looks close to saturated, saturation, and sate, and sits near soak and drench.
note.cn: saturate 是表示「装满」的动词：形近于 saturated、saturation 与 sate，近义上有 soak、fill 等词。

entries.definition: full of liquid or filled to the limit
entries.definitionCN: 浸透的；饱和的

entries.definition: the state of being completely full
entries.definitionCN: 饱和状态；浸透

entries.definition: to satisfy fully, sometimes to the point of weariness
entries.definitionCN: 使饱足，有时指吃腻了

entries.definition: to make something very wet by leaving it in liquid
entries.definitionCN: 浸泡；使湿透

entries.definition: to put as much as possible into a container
entries.definitionCN: 装满

entries.definition: to make someone or something completely wet
entries.definitionCN: 使湿透

normalIntro.en: Saturate is built on Latin satur, full; think of a sponge that can hold no more water.
normalIntro.cn: saturate 来自拉丁语 satur（饱的、满满的）；想象一块再也吸不进水分的海绵。

normal.en: The -ate ending marks a verb, so saturate is the action of filling to the limit.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标明它是动词，所以 saturate 是「填到满」的动作。

normal.en: Saturated fat and saturated solution are common set phrases in science.
normal.cn: saturated fat 与 saturated solution 是科学中常见的固定说法。

normal.en: Saturate the market means to have made too many products for buyers.
normal.cn: saturate the market 指产品多到买家消化不了。

normal.en: Be saturated with links the verb to the thing doing the filling.
normal.cn: be saturated with 把动词与起填充作用的东西连接起来。

normal.en: Compare soak: soak is everyday and wet, while saturate is more technical and complete.
normal.cn: 对比 soak：soak 日常而偏湿，saturate 更技术化，也更强调彻底。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge dripping because the water cannot get in any further.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵正在滴水，因为再也吸不进更多水分。

abstract.en: Imagine shelves so packed that a new box has no place to stand.
abstract.cn: 想象货架塞得满满，新来的盒子无处可放。

abstract.en: Think of a room where the smell of coffee reaches every corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，咖啡的香味渗到每个角落。

examples.en: The spring rain had saturated the soil before noon.
examples.cn: 春雨到中午前就已浸透了土壤。

examples.en: Cheap clothing imports quickly saturate the domestic market.
examples.cn: 廉价服装进口很快让国内市场饱和。

examples.en: The river is saturated with industrial waste.
examples.cn: 这条河里充满了工业废料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞出瑞特」——塞得太满，一点空隙都不留；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 satur（饱的、满满的）→ saturare（填满）→ saturatus（已填满的）→ 英语 saturate；核心义「填到再装不下」。

sensesIntro.en: Saturate begins with liquid soaking in, then grows into any supply that is full, an atmosphere that is everywhere, a technical limit, and a colour at its peak.
sensesIntro.cn: saturate 从液体浸透开始，再扩展到任何装满的供应、弥漫到处处的氛围、技术上的极限，以及颜色最浓的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sponge that has taken in water until it drips.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块吸满水、直往下滴的海绵。

branches.en: Wet through is the physical sense of filling with liquid.
branches.cn: 湿透是「用液体填满」的物理义。

branches.en: A market with no room left is the supply sense.
branches.cn: 再无余量的市场是供应层面的义项。

branches.en: Filling every part of a place gives the atmosphere sense.
branches.cn: 填满一个地方的每个部分，得到「弥漫」义。

branches.en: A channel carrying the maximum gives the technical limit sense.
branches.cn: 通道承载到最大值，得到技术上的极限义。

branches.en: Both a full market and a full colour have reached their peak.
branches.cn: 饱和的市场和饱和的颜色都达到了各自的峰值。

intro.en: Saturate belongs to the Latin satur family; English builds saturation, saturated, and supersaturate around it.
intro.cn: saturate 属于拉丁语 satur 一族；英语围绕它构成 saturation、saturated 与 supersaturate。

latinIntro.en: Latin satur means full, saturare means to fill, and saturatus is the finished, filled state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satur 意为饱的，saturare 意为填满，saturatus 意为已填满的状态。

items.example: Satur gives the core idea of fullness.
items.exampleCN: satur 提供「满」这一核心观念。

items.example: Saturare is the direct source verb.
items.exampleCN: saturare 是直接的来源动词。

items.example: The suffix -ate turns fullness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把「满」变成动作。

items.example: Saturate keeps the filling sense.
items.exampleCN: saturate 保留「填满」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms saturation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 saturation。

items.example: Saturation names the full state.
items.exampleCN: saturation 指「满」的状态。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms saturated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 saturated。

items.example: The prefix super- adds the idea of going beyond full.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 super- 加上「超过满」的意思。

items.meaning: to fill beyond the normal limit
items.example: Supersaturate describes an unstable excess.
items.exampleCN: supersaturate 描述不稳定的过量状态。

latinEntries.meaning: a mixed dish; a medley of verses
latinEntries.meaningCN: 大拼盘；杂咏（英语 satire 的远源）

definition_zh: 品尝；玩味；细细品味；滋味；风味
definition_en: to enjoy the taste or quality of something slowly and fully
core_image: 闭上眼，把一口汤含在舌尖很久才咽下
scene: 老人在小花园里摘下一颗熟透的番茄，先闻一闻，再慢慢咬下去，让汁水在嘴里停一会儿。The old gardener picked a ripe tomato. He savoured it in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 savour 是「细细品尝」（第 1 个义项：慢慢地尝出食物的味道）；句意：老园丁摘下一颗熟透的番茄，在阳光下细细享受它的味道。

derivatives.zh: 由 savour 加 -y 构成，义为「咸香的；开胃的」
过去分词用作形容词，义为「被细细品味的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 savoury 构成，义为「令人不快的；名声不好的」

senses.title: To taste food slowly and fully
senses.definition: to eat or drink something slowly so as to enjoy its taste completely
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢地吃或喝某物，以便充分享受它的味道
senses.example: She savoured the soup before saying a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她先细细品尝了那碗汤，才开口说话。
senses.why: Old French savour means taste, and to savour is to give that taste the time it needs to be felt.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 savour 意为「味道」，而 savour 就是给这个味道留出足够的感受时间。

senses.title: To enjoy an experience intensely
senses.definition: to enjoy a moment, feeling, or success as fully as possible
senses.definitionCN: 尽可能地充分享受某个时刻、感受或成功
senses.example: The team savoured their first win of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 全队尽情享受着本赛季的第一场胜利。
senses.why: A good taste on the tongue need not come from food, so people savour praise, music, or a quiet evening in the same slow way.
senses.whyCN: 舌头上的好滋味不必来自食物，所以人们也会用同样缓慢的方式去品味赞美、音乐或一个安静的夜晚。

senses.title: To dwell on an idea with pleasure
senses.definition: to think about or recall something with lingering enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 带着久久不散的愉悦去思考或回想某事
senses.example: He savoured the memory of that afternoon for years.
senses.exampleCN: 那天的记忆让他回味了很多年。
senses.why: Savour slows time down; applied to thought, it becomes the pleasure of turning an idea or memory over again.
senses.whyCN: savour 让时间慢下来；用于思维时，它就变成反复琢磨一个念头或一段回忆的乐趣。

senses.title: A distinct taste or flavour
senses.definition: the particular taste or quality that something has, often in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 某物特有的味道或品质，多见于文学性表达
senses.example: The bread had the savour of wood smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 那面包带着柴火的烟熏味。
senses.why: The noun keeps the Old French sense directly: savour is the taste itself, not the act of tasting it.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接保留了古法语的本义：savour 就是味道本身，而不是品尝的动作。

senses.title: A trace of character or interest
senses.definition: a quality that gives something special character or appeal, or a good reputation
senses.definitionCN: 使某物有特别色彩或引力的品质，也可指好名声
senses.example: Her writing has lost none of its savour.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文字丝毫未失往日的情趣。
senses.why: From a literal taste, savour extends to whatever gives life its relish, so old texts also use it for good name and standing.
senses.whyCN: 从字面上的味道出发，savour 又扩展到让生活有滋有味的东西，因此旧时文本也用指好名声与声望。

intro.en: Savour comes from Latin sapor by way of Old French savour, and simply means taste.
intro.cn: savour 经由古法语 savour 来自拉丁语 sapor，本义就是「味道」。

items.en: Sapor means taste or flavour, from sapere, to taste and to be wise.
items.cn: sapor 意为味道、风味，来自 sapere（尝出味道，也表示有见识）。

items.en: Savour brings the noun into French with the meaning of taste.
items.cn: savour 把这个名词带入法语，意为味道。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English first as a noun for flavour.
items.cn: 该词在中古英语中先以名词身份出现，指风味。

items.en: The verb to savour grows from the noun, meaning to taste or to give flavour.
items.cn: 动词用法从名词发展而来，16 至 17 世纪起意为「品尝、调味」。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of enjoying an experience slowly, and the American spelling savor.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「慢慢享受经历」的引申义，并出现美式拼写 savor。

note.en: Savour is the slow enjoyment of taste: it looks close to savoury and savor, and sits near taste, relish, and delight in meaning.
note.cn: savour 指对味道的慢慢享受：形近于 savoury 与美式拼写 savor，近义上有 taste、relish、delight 等词。

entries.definition: salty or spicy rather than sweet, as spelled with -or in the United States
entries.definitionCN: 咸香的，美式拼写，对应英式 savoury

entries.definition: having a pleasant salty or spicy taste
entries.definitionCN: 咸香的；开胃的

entries.definition: having no taste or flavour
entries.definitionCN: 没有味道的；平淡无味的

entries.definition: to notice the flavour of food in your mouth
entries.definitionCN: 尝；品尝

entries.definition: to enjoy something greatly
entries.definitionCN: 享受；喜爱

entries.definition: to drink in small amounts
entries.definitionCN: 小口地喝

normalIntro.en: Savour is the noun for taste turned into a slow verb; its British -our spelling is the key to recognising it.
normalIntro.cn: savour 就是「味道」这个名词变成了动作缓慢的动词；记住英式的 -our 拼写就能认出来。

normal.en: The -our spelling is British; American English writes savor.
normal.cn: 英式拼写是 -our，美式写作 savor。

normal.en: Savour the moment is a very common phrase of praise for good times.
normal.cn: savour the moment 是赞美美好时光的常见说法。

normal.en: Savoury is the adjective for food that is salty rather than sweet.
normal.cn: savoury 是形容咸味而非甜味食物的形容词。

normal.en: The negative un- in unsavoury turns a good taste into a bad reputation.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 un- 加在 unsavoury 上，把「好味道」变成了坏名声。

normal.en: Compare taste: taste is neutral and quick, savour adds care and pleasure.
normal.cn: 对比 taste：taste 中性而快速，savour 多了用心与愉悦。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon held in the mouth a little longer than usual.
abstract.cn: 想象一只勺子停在嘴里，比平常多停了一会儿。

abstract.en: Imagine replaying a favourite song once more just for the last line.
abstract.cn: 想象为了最后一句又把最喜欢的歌再放一遍。

abstract.en: Think of keeping a good memory on the tongue like a sweet.
abstract.cn: 想象把一段美好的回忆像糖一样含在舌头上。

examples.en: Take your time and savour the coffee.
examples.cn: 别着急，慢慢品味这杯咖啡。

examples.en: They savoured every minute of the holiday.
examples.cn: 他们享受着假期的每一分钟。

examples.en: The stew has a rich savour of herbs.
examples.cn: 这锅炖菜有浓郁的香草味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞味儿」——把味道塞进嘴里细细感受；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sapere（尝出味道）→ sapor（味道）→ 古法语 savour（味道）→ 中古英语 savour（风味）→ 英语 savour（品尝；品味）。

sensesIntro.en: Savour starts as a noun for taste, becomes a verb of savouring food, then of savouring any experience, and finally returns to noun senses of flavour and character.
sensesIntro.cn: savour 起初是表示味道的名词，后来变成品尝食物的动词，再引申为享受任何经历，最后又回到表示风味与意味的名词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouth holding one spoonful a long time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺汤在嘴里停留很久。

branches.en: Tasting food slowly is the first verb sense.
branches.cn: 慢慢品尝食物是第一个动词义项。

branches.en: Enjoying an experience is the transferred sense.
branches.cn: 享受一段经历是转移后的引申义。

branches.en: Turning an idea over with pleasure is the mind sense.
branches.cn: 在脑中反复琢磨是思维层面的义项。

branches.en: The taste itself survives as a literary noun.
branches.cn: 味道本身作为文学性名词保留下来。

branches.en: Both a flavour and a reputation give something its character.
branches.cn: 风味和名声都赋予某物以独特气质。

intro.en: Savour comes from the Latin sapor family; English builds savoury, savourless, and unsavoury around it.
intro.cn: savour 来自拉丁语 sapor 一族；英语围绕它构成 savoury、savourless 与 unsavoury。

latinIntro.en: Latin sapere means to taste or to be wise, and sapor is the taste itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sapere 意为尝出味道、有见识，sapor 则是味道本身。

items.example: Sapere carries both taste and wisdom.
items.exampleCN: sapere 兼有「味道」与「智慧」两层意思。

items.example: Sapor is the direct Latin noun source.
items.exampleCN: sapor 是直接的拉丁名词来源。

items.meaningCN: 源自法语的 -or 的英式写法
items.example: The -our spelling follows French pronunciation habits.
items.exampleCN: -our 拼写沿袭法语的习惯。

items.example: Savour keeps both the noun and the verb.
items.exampleCN: savour 名词与动词两种身份都在。

items.example: The suffix -y forms savoury.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 savoury。

items.example: Savoury describes food with a strong taste.
items.exampleCN: savoury 形容味道浓郁的咸味食物。

items.example: The suffix -less forms savourless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 savourless。

items.example: The prefix un- negates savoury.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使 savoury 变为否定。

items.meaningCN: 令人不快的；名声不好的
items.example: Unsavoury often describes people or stories.
items.exampleCN: unsavoury 常用来形容人或事情。

definition_zh: 萨克斯管；萨克斯风（一种金属管体、单簧片发声的管乐器）
definition_en: a metal wind instrument with a reed mouthpiece and a curved body, used in jazz and military bands
core_image: 舞台上弯曲的铜管乐手吹响萨克斯
scene: 深夜的酒吧里，灯光昏黄，乐手站在小舞台上，把弯弯的金属管子举到嘴边，空气里立刻飘出慵懒的旋律。The saxophone glowed under the dim lights. The band played a slow tune.
sceneCN: 这里 saxophone 是「萨克斯管」（第 1 个义项：一种用单簧片发声的金属管乐器）；句意：萨克斯管在昏暗的灯下发亮，乐队奏着一支缓慢的曲子。

derivatives.zh: 由 saxophone 加 -ist 构成，义为「萨克斯手」
saxophone 的口语截短形式，义为「萨克斯」
由 saxophone 加 -ic 构成，较少见的形容词，义为「萨克斯风的」

senses.title: A curved reed wind instrument
senses.definition: a metal wind instrument with a single reed and a curved body that makes a warm, powerful sound
senses.definitionCN: 一种管体弯曲、以单簧片发声的金属管乐器，音色温暖而有力
senses.example: She has played the saxophone since she was twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 她从十二岁起就开始吹萨克斯管。
senses.why: Sax was its inventor, and -phone means sound, so the name literally labels a sound-making metal tube.
senses.whyCN: Sax 是发明者的姓，-phone 意为「声音」，所以这个名字字面上就是「发出声音的金属管」。

senses.title: The voice of jazz
senses.definition: the saxophone as a symbol of jazz and jazz-style improvisation
senses.definitionCN: 作为爵士乐即兴风格象征的萨克斯管
senses.example: The saxophone became the voice of jazz in the roaring twenties.
senses.exampleCN: 萨克斯管在二十年代的爵士乐中成了标志性嗓音。
senses.why: Its strong sound suits jazz improvisation, so the instrument came to stand for the music itself.
senses.whyCN: 它洪亮的音色适合爵士即兴演奏，于是这件乐器成为这种音乐本身的象征。

senses.title: A member of the band family
senses.definition: any one of the family of differently sized saxophones, from soprano to bass
senses.definitionCN: 萨克斯家族中任一尺寸的乐器，从中音到低音不等
senses.example: The orchestra borrowed four saxophones for the piece.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团为这首作品借了四支萨克斯。
senses.why: Like a family of voices, the saxophone comes in several sizes, and each gets a different pitch.
senses.whyCN: 像不同的嗓音一样，萨克斯也有多种尺寸，每种尺寸音高不同。

senses.title: A saxophone sound or part
senses.definition: a saxophone line in a piece of music, or the sound a saxophone makes
senses.definitionCN: 乐曲中的萨克斯声部，或萨克斯发出的声音
senses.example: The opening saxophone sets the mood for the film.
senses.exampleCN: 开场的萨克斯声音为影片定下基调。
senses.why: Players talk about the saxophone part, so the word also names that line or that sound in a score.
senses.whyCN: 乐手会说萨克斯声部，因此这个词也用来指乐谱里的那一行或那种音色。

intro.en: Saxophone was coined in 1840s Paris from the name of its inventor, Adolphe Sax, plus Greek phone, meaning sound.
intro.cn: saxophone 于十九世纪四十年代在巴黎被创造出来，由发明者阿道夫·萨克斯的姓氏 Sax 加上希腊语 phone（声音）构成。

items.en: Phone means voice or sound.
items.cn: phone 意为嗓音、声音。

items.en: The Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax perfects the instrument in Paris.
items.cn: 比利时乐器制造者阿道夫·萨克斯在巴黎完善了这种乐器。

items.en: The surname Sax joins the suffix -phone to name the new instrument.
items.cn: 姓氏 Sax 与词缀 -phone 结合，为新乐器命名。

items.en: The word enters English and is soon shortened to sax in speech.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，口语中很快缩略为 sax。

items.en: Jazz makes the saxophone a household sound of the twentieth century.
items.cn: 爵士乐让萨克斯管成为二十世纪家喻户晓的声音。

note.en: Saxophone names an instrument: it is built from sax and -phone, so its family looks like sax, saxophonist, and other words ending in -phone.
note.cn: saxophone 是一件乐器的名称：它由 sax 与 -phone 构成，因此词族包括 sax、saxophonist 以及其它以 -phone 结尾的词。

entries.definition: a short informal word for saxophone
entries.definitionCN: saxophone 的口语简称

entries.definition: a person who plays the saxophone
entries.definitionCN: 萨克斯手

entries.definition: a family of brass instruments invented by the same maker, not a reed instrument
entries.definitionCN: 由同一发明者设计的铜管族乐器，并非簧片乐器；只是拼写相近，来源同一姓氏而形制不同

entries.definition: a straight wooden reed instrument with a much softer, narrower sound
entries.definitionCN: 直身的木质单簧管，音色更软更窄

entries.definition: a brass instrument played without a reed
entries.definitionCN: 不用簧片的铜管小号

entries.definition: a small hand-held reed instrument used in blues
entries.definitionCN: 布鲁斯里常见的口琴

normalIntro.en: Saxophone is built from the name Sax plus Greek phone, sound, so the word carries its inventor and its function at once.
normalIntro.cn: saxophone 由姓氏 Sax 加希腊语 phone（声音）构成，所以这个词同时带着发明者和它的功能。

normal.en: The capital S in Sax reminds you of Adolphe Sax, the inventor.
normal.cn: Sax 的首字母大写 S 能提醒你发明者阿道夫·萨克斯。

normal.en: Compare telephone and microphone: the -phone also means sound.
normal.cn: 对比 telephone 与 microphone，-phone 同样表示「声音」。

normal.en: Saxophonist adds -ist to name the player of the instrument.
normal.cn: saxophonist 加 -ist 表示演奏这件乐器的人。

normal.en: Play the saxophone uses the definite article with instruments, unlike play football.
normal.cn: play the saxophone 在乐器前带定冠词，与 play football 不同。

normal.en: Compare clarinet: both use a single reed, but only the saxophone has a metal body.
normal.cn: 对比 clarinet：两者都用单簧片，但只有萨克斯是金属管体。

abstract.en: Picture a curved brass tube curling back toward the player mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯曲的铜管，弯回去伸向乐手的嘴边。

abstract.en: Hear a warm tenor line floating under a smoky bar light.
abstract.cn: 听见一段温暖的次中音旋律，在昏暗的酒吧灯下飘着。

abstract.en: See the letters S-A-X shining on the bell of the instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象乐器喇叭口上闪着 S A X 三个字母。

examples.en: He plays the saxophone in a small jazz band.
examples.cn: 他在一个小爵士乐队里吹萨克斯管。

examples.en: The shop sells saxophones and clarinets.
examples.cn: 这家店出售萨克斯管和单簧管。

examples.en: A saxophone solo closed the concert.
examples.cn: 一场萨克斯独奏为音乐会画上句号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞克斯风」——塞住簧片吹出风声；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 发明者姓氏 Sax（阿道夫·萨克斯）+ 希腊语 phone（声音）→ 法语 saxophone → 英语 saxophone；核心义「以萨克斯之名发声的金属管乐器」。

sensesIntro.en: Saxophone first names one instrument, then grows into a jazz symbol, the whole family of sizes, and finally any saxophone line or sound.
sensesIntro.cn: saxophone 先指一件具体的乐器，再引申为爵士乐象征、整个家族的不同尺寸，最后指乐曲中的萨克斯声部或音色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved metal tube blown with a reed mouthpiece.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯曲的金属管，用簧片吹响。

branches.en: One physical instrument is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 一件实体乐器是基本义项。

branches.en: A jazz symbol is the cultural extension.
branches.cn: 爵士象征是文化层面的延伸。

branches.en: The whole family of sizes widens the reference.
branches.cn: 不同尺寸的整个家族扩大了所指范围。

branches.en: A musical line or sound is the abstract use.
branches.cn: 乐谱声部或音色是抽象用法。

branches.en: The object and its sound are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 乐器本身与它发出的声音由同一个词来表示。

intro.en: Saxophone combines a surname with a Greek sound element; English adds sax and saxophonist around it.
intro.cn: saxophone 由一个姓氏加上表示「声音」的希腊语成分构成；英语围绕它构成 sax 与 saxophonist。

latinIntro.en: The -phone part goes back to Greek phone, voice or sound; the name Sax is French and has no Latin source of its own.
latinIntro.cn: -phone 部分可追到希腊语 phone（声音）；名字部分 Sax 是法语姓氏，本身没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Sax fixes the instrument to one inventor.
items.exampleCN: Sax 把乐器与发明者绑定在一起。

items.example: The -phone element says the thing makes sound.
items.exampleCN: -phone 这一成分表明它发出声音。

items.example: Saxophone keeps the original coined name.
items.exampleCN: saxophone 保留了最初的新造名称。

items.meaning: an informal word for the instrument
items.example: Sax is the clipped form used in speech.
items.exampleCN: sax 是口语中截短的叫法。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms saxophonist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 saxophonist。

items.example: Saxophonist names the player.
items.exampleCN: saxophonist 指演奏者。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms saxophonic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 saxophonic。

items.meaning: person and quality endings used together
items.meaningCN: 「人」与「性质」两个词尾的组合模式
items.example: Both endings keep the family clear.
items.exampleCN: 这两个词尾让词族关系一目了然。

items.meaning: high, used for a medium-pitched saxophone
items.meaningCN: 高，用作中音萨克斯管的名称部分
items.example: Alto saxophone names the most common size.
items.exampleCN: alto saxophone 指最常见的尺寸。

definition_zh: 烫伤；焯水；用沸水消毒；烫洗
definition_en: to burn the skin with hot liquid or steam, or to wash, clean, or cook something with boiling water
core_image: 一壶沸水翻倒，白汽腾起，皮肤上立刻红起一片
scene: 厨房里水壶刚烧开，孩子伸手去抓把手，大人一把按住壶身。The steam scalded his hand before he could pull away.
sceneCN: 这里 scald 是「烫伤」（第 1 个义项：被滚烫的液体或蒸汽烫到皮肤）；句意：他还没来得及缩手，蒸汽就把手烫伤了。可辨识画面：翻倒的水壶、升起的白汽、缩回的手。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加分词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「滚烫的；灼人的」，也作名词表示烫伤
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被烫过的；焯过水的」
由动词加表人或表物的 -er 构成，指从事烫洗工作的人或设备

senses.title: To burn skin with very hot liquid
senses.definition: to hurt or burn the skin with boiling water, hot oil, or steam
senses.definitionCN: 用沸水、热油或蒸汽伤害或灼伤皮肤
senses.example: She scalded her fingers on the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 她被水壶烫伤了手指。
senses.why: The Latin source means to wash in hot water, and the heat that cleans easily goes one step too far and burns.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语源头意为「用热水洗」，洗东西的热水稍一过热就变成了灼伤。

senses.title: To rinse or disinfect with boiling water
senses.definition: to pour boiling water over something, often a container, in order to clean or sterilize it
senses.definitionCN: 把沸水浇在容器等物上，以求清洁或消毒
senses.example: Scald the jars before you fill them with jam.
senses.exampleCN: 装果酱之前先用沸水烫一遍罐子。
senses.why: The oldest use is exactly washing in very hot water; kitchen hygiene keeps this cleaning sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法就是「用很热的水洗」，厨房卫生习惯让这个清洗义项一直保留下来。

senses.title: To plunge food into boiling water
senses.definition: to put food briefly into boiling water so that it softens, loosens its skin, or loses a raw taste
senses.definitionCN: 把食物短暂放进沸水里，使其变软、去皮或去掉生味
senses.example: Scald the tomatoes for ten seconds, then peel them.
senses.exampleCN: 把番茄烫十秒，然后去皮。
senses.why: Cooking turns the washing idea inside out: the hot water now works on the food itself rather than on dirt.
senses.whyCN: 烹调把「洗」的思路反过来用：热水不再去除污垢，而是作用在食物本身。

senses.title: A burn caused by hot liquid
senses.definition: an injury to the skin caused by very hot liquid or steam
senses.definitionCN: 由极热的液体或蒸汽造成的皮肤损伤
senses.example: The nurse cleaned the scald on his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给他清洗了手臂上的烫伤。
senses.why: Once the verb describes the damage, the noun can name that damage as a thing you can see and treat.
senses.whyCN: 动词描述造成损害的过程，名词便可以把这处损害当成看得见、可以处理的伤口来指称。

senses.title: To heat a liquid almost to boiling
senses.definition: to heat milk or another liquid until it is just below boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 把牛奶等液体加热到接近沸腾的程度
senses.example: Scald the milk, then let it cool slightly.
senses.exampleCN: 把牛奶加热到将沸，再稍放凉。
senses.why: From washing with hot water comes a milder use: bringing a liquid near the boil without letting it boil over.
senses.whyCN: 从「用热水洗」延伸出一种更温和的用法：把液体加热到接近沸点，却不让它翻滚溢出。

intro.en: Scald comes from Latin excaldare, to bathe in hot water, through the northern French form escalder.
intro.cn: scald 来自拉丁语 excaldare（用热水沐浴），经北方法语形式 escalder 进入英语。

items.en: Excaldare means to bathe or soak in hot water.
items.cn: excaldare 意为用热水沐浴或浸泡。

items.en: In popular speech the first syllable drops, leaving caldus, hot.
items.cn: 在通俗拉丁语中首音节脱落，留下表示「热的」caldus。

items.en: Northern French escalder and eschalder carry the washing sense north.
items.cn: 北方法语的 escalder、eschalder 把「用热水洗」的含义带到北方。

items.en: Scalden appears in cooking and household texts with the meaning of washing in boiling water.
items.cn: 中古英语 scalden 出现在烹饪与家务文献中，意思是「用开水烫洗」。

items.en: The washing sense narrows, and the word comes to mean the burn itself.
items.cn: 到十六七世纪，烫洗的含义收窄，词义转为指烫伤本身。

items.en: Modern English keeps both halves: the burn, and the careful use of hot water.
items.cn: 现代英语把两面都保留下来：既有烫伤，也有谨慎地使用热水。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same French family or with the same spelling pattern; the near-meaning group holds the other words of heat and cooking.
note.cn: 形近组收同一法语来源的同族词以及拼写相近的词；近义组收表示加热与烹调的相邻词。

entries.definition: so hot that it burns or hurts
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，由 scald 加 -ing 构成，义为「滚烫的」。

entries.definition: a thin plate on fish skin, or a device for weighing
entries.definitionCN: 义为「鱼鳞」或「秤」，只是拼写与 scald 相近，词源不同（scale 来自斯堪的纳维亚语 skal）。

entries.definition: an old unit of measure for coal
entries.definitionCN: 义为旧时的煤量单位，与 scald 共享表示「热」的拉丁语 caldus，只是同源，意义已无关。

entries.definition: to damage the skin with fire, heat, or chemicals
entries.definitionCN: 义为「烧伤」，范围比 scald 宽，火焰、化学物都可算。

entries.definition: to singe the surface of something with dry heat
entries.definitionCN: 义为「灼焦表面」，多用干热而不是液体。

entries.definition: to boil vegetables briefly and then cool them
entries.definitionCN: 义为「焯」，与表示焯水的 scald 几乎同义，侧重焯后过凉水。

normalIntro.en: Scald is hot water going one degree too far: washing turns into burning.
normalIntro.cn: scald 是热水多热了一点：本来是洗，结果变成了烫。

normal.en: Scald on the kettle and scald the jars are the same verb in two directions.
normal.cn: scald on the kettle 和 scald the jars 是同一个动词的两个方向：一个烫人，一个烫物。

normal.en: Scalding water is the collocation that keeps the heat image sharp.
normal.cn: 搭配 scalding water 让「滚烫」这一意象一直保持清晰。

normal.en: To scald milk is to stop just short of boiling, so heat and caution sit in one word.
normal.cn: scald milk 指加热到将沸就停，所以这个词里同时有热与谨慎。

normal.en: In the kitchen, blanch and scald are neighbours: both plunge food into boiling water briefly.
normal.cn: 在厨房里 blanch 与 scald 是邻居：两者都把食物短时间放进沸水。

normal.en: Keep the fifth letter: scald has a d at the end, while scale ends in e.
normal.cn: 记住末尾的字母 d：scald 以 d 结尾，scale 以 e 结尾。

abstract.en: Picture steam rising from a lid and a hand snapping back too late.
abstract.cn: 想象锅盖边升起白汽，手缩回时已经晚了一步。

abstract.en: Picture boiling water poured over glass jars on a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房桌上，沸水浇在玻璃罐上腾起白雾。

abstract.en: Picture a tomato dropped into a pot for a few seconds, its skin splitting at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗番茄在锅里只待了几秒，顶上的皮就裂开了。

examples.en: The child scalded himself on the hot soup.
examples.cn: 孩子被热汤烫伤了。

examples.en: Scald the tomatoes briefly before peeling them.
examples.cn: 剥皮前先把番茄快速烫一下。

examples.en: He wrapped a cool cloth round the scald on his wrist.
examples.cn: 他在手腕的烫伤上裹了一块凉布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「死烤的」——沸水泼到皮肤上，像被烤焦了一小片。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 excaldare（用热水沐浴）→ 通俗拉丁语 caldus（热的）→ 北方法语 escalder、eschalder（用热水烫洗）→ 中古英语 scalden → 现代英语 scald，核心由「热水洗」转为「被热水所伤」。

sensesIntro.en: Scald begins with hot water used to wash, which is why it covers both the burn and the careful boiling of water, milk, or food.
sensesIntro.cn: scald 的起点是用热水烫洗，因此既指着热水造成的伤害，也指用沸水处理器物、牛奶与食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boiling water tips over and a patch of skin turns red, steam still rising.
core.cn: 核心意象：沸水泼翻，一片皮肤立刻发红，白汽还在往上冒。

branches.en: A hand pulls away from the kettle too late is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 手从水壶上缩回却已经太晚，这就是日常最常用的义项。

branches.en: Jars scalded before jam is the oldest cleaning sense.
branches.cn: 装果酱前烫一遍罐子，这是最古老的清洁义项。

branches.en: A tomato in boiling water is the cooking sense.
branches.cn: 番茄下沸水，这是烹调义项。

branches.en: The burn and the wound it leaves are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 烫的过程与留下的伤口，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: Both clean containers and hot milk call for heat that is held just at the edge.
branches.cn: 烫罐子与加热牛奶都要求把热控制在临界点上。

intro.en: Scald is a Latin verb cut down in French, and English builds scald, scalding, and scalded on that stem.
intro.cn: scald 是一个在法语中被削短的拉丁语动词，英语在它上面构成 scald、scalding 与 scalded。

latinIntro.en: Latin calere means to be hot; excaldare means to bathe in hot water, and caldus means hot.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calere 意为发热，excaldare 意为用热水沐浴，caldus 意为热的。

items.example: Calere holds the heat that runs through the family.
items.exampleCN: calere 带着贯穿这一族词的「热」。

items.example: Caldus is the popular form used in everyday Latin.
items.exampleCN: caldus 是拉丁语口语中常用的形式。

items.example: The prefix ex- strengthens the act of bathing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 强化了沐浴这个动作。

items.example: Excaldare is the direct ancestor of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: excaldare 是英语动词的直接祖先。

items.example: Eschalder is the northern French form that reached England.
items.exampleCN: eschalder 是传到英格兰的北方法语形式。

items.example: Scald keeps the verb sense in English.
items.exampleCN: scald 在英语中保留了动词用法。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词与名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms scalding.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 scalding。

items.example: Scalding describes water that hurts to touch.
items.exampleCN: scalding 形容碰不得的热水。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms scalder.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 scalder。

items.meaning: a person or device that scalds
items.meaningCN: 做烫洗工作的人或设备
items.example: Scalder names the agent of the action.
items.exampleCN: scalder 指这一动作的执行者。

definition_zh: 蹦跳；轻快地跑来跑去；急速奔跑
definition_en: to run with quick, light steps, often in play or in a hurry, like a small animal
core_image: 一只小松鼠在树根与落叶间连蹦带跳地窜过
scene: 公园的长椅上，一只松鼠叼着坚果，尾巴一甩就窜进灌木丛。A squirrel scampered up the tree with a nut in its mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 scamper 是「连蹦带跳地跑」（第 1 个义项：步子小而快、一跳一跳地跑开）；句意：一只松鼠叼着坚果，一蹦一跳地爬上了树。可辨识画面：长椅、叼着坚果的松鼠、蹿进树丛的身影。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「蹦跳奔跑的动作或声响」，也可作形容词
由动词加表人的 -er 构成，义为「奔跑轻快者」，多指小孩或小动物
拼写同源但意义分化，常指「淘气鬼；小流氓」，与奔跑义无直接关系

senses.title: To run with light, quick steps
senses.definition: to move quickly with small, light steps, especially with a hopping motion
senses.definitionCN: 以小而轻的步子快速移动，尤指带一点跳跃感
senses.example: The children scampered across the lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们蹦蹦跳跳地跑过草坪。
senses.why: The word names a hurried, bouncing run, so the steps stay short while the speed stays high.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来指匆忙又弹跳的奔跑，所以步子很短，速度却很快。

senses.title: To run off in fright or haste
senses.definition: to run away quickly, especially when startled or eager to leave
senses.definitionCN: 迅速跑开，尤指受到惊吓或急于离开时
senses.example: The cat scampered off when the gate banged.
senses.exampleCN: 门一响，猫便一溜烟跑开了。
senses.why: Small animals run fastest when they are escaping, so the playful step takes on a note of alarm.
senses.whyCN: 小动物受惊时跑得最快，于是这种轻快的步子也多了一层惊慌的意味。

senses.title: To climb up in quick little bursts
senses.definition: to move up a tree, a slope, or a similar surface with short rapid scrambling steps
senses.definitionCN: 以小而急促的步子爬树、上坡或在类似的表面上快速上行
senses.example: Squirrels scamper to the top of the oak in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 松鼠几秒钟就能蹿到橡树顶上。
senses.why: Because the step is small and light, it suits climbing without a long stride, which explains the up direction.
senses.whyCN: 正因为步子小而轻、不需要长距离跨步，它才特别适合向上攀爬，这解释了为什么常带上方位词。

senses.title: A light running step or its sound
senses.titleCN: 轻快的奔跑（动作或声响）
senses.definition: the act or sound of light, quick running, especially of small feet
senses.definitionCN: 轻快奔跑的动作或声响，尤指小脚丫跑动的声音
senses.example: We heard a scamper across the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听到门厅里一阵细碎的跑动声。
senses.why: The verb has a matching noun, so the quick little steps can be heard and named as one short burst.
senses.whyCN: 动词有相应的名词形式，所以那一阵快速的碎步声可以被听见，并被整体地指称出来。

intro.en: Scamper is of uncertain origin; it is first recorded in English around the late sixteenth century.
intro.cn: scamper 的来源不确定，英语中约在十六世纪后期首次出现。

items.en: Many scholars link it to a Germanic run base also seen in scamp, but this is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 许多学者把它联系到与 scamp 同源的日耳曼语「跑」词干，但这只是重构形式。

items.en: Scamper first appears in print with the sense of running hastily about.
items.cn: scamper 在十六世纪九十年代首次见于书面，意为匆忙乱跑。

items.en: The meaning narrows to light, quick, often playful steps.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，词义收窄为轻快、迅捷、常带嬉戏意味的步子。

items.en: Writers apply the verb to small animals and insects, not only to people.
items.cn: 十八世纪的作者把这个动词用在小型动物和昆虫身上，不再只写人。

items.en: Scamper keeps the light and hasty sense and now often describes children and pets.
items.cn: 现代英语保持「轻快而匆忙」的含义，如今常用来写小孩和宠物。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the related verb and its derivatives; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of quick movement.
note.cn: 形近组收相关动词及其派生词；近义组收表示快速移动的相邻动词。

entries.definition: moving with quick light steps
entries.definitionCN: 由 scamper 加 -ing 构成，义为「蹦跳奔跑的」，也可作名词。

entries.definition: a dishonest or mischievous person, or to do work carelessly
entries.definitionCN: 义为「淘气鬼；胡闹做事」，一般认为与 scamper 同源，意义已分化。

entries.definition: large prawns cooked in garlic and butter
entries.definitionCN: 义为大蒜黄油焗大虾，只是拼写与 scamper 相近，词源不同（来自意大利语 scampi）。

entries.definition: to move quickly on foot with long or steady strides
entries.definitionCN: 义为「跑」，最通用的说法，不含轻快蹦跳的感觉。

entries.definition: to move suddenly and very fast over a short distance
entries.definitionCN: 义为「猛冲、蹿」，强调突然与极快，距离短。

entries.definition: to move quickly with short steps, often in alarm
entries.definitionCN: 义为「小步急走」，与 scamper 最近，但更侧重慌张而不侧重蹦跳。

normalIntro.en: Scamper is the sound and shape of tiny feet taking short, fast, bouncing steps.
normalIntro.cn: scamper 就是小脚丫又短又快的步子，连同那阵哒哒声。

normal.en: The verb is often followed by a direction: scamper up, scamper off, scamper away.
normal.cn: 这个动词后常接方向：scamper up、scamper off、scamper away。

normal.en: Scamper about keeps the sense of restless, playful movement.
normal.cn: 搭配 scamper about 保留了「不安分、嬉戏」的动感。

normal.en: Squirrels and mice are the classic subjects, because small legs take small steps fast.
normal.cn: 松鼠和老鼠是它的经典对象，因为小腿步子小、频率快。

normal.en: Compare scurry: scurry is anxious and flat, scamper is bouncy and light.
normal.cn: 对比 scurry：scurry 带慌张且贴地，scamper 轻快而有弹跳感。

normal.en: The noun scamper names one short burst of that running, as in a scamper across the hall.
normal.cn: 名词 scamper 指那一阵短促的跑动，例如一阵跑过门厅的碎步声。

abstract.en: Picture a squirrel with a nut, three bounces and gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只叼着坚果的松鼠，连跳三下就不见了。

abstract.en: Picture bare feet crossing a cold stone floor in quick, tiny leaps.
abstract.cn: 想象光脚丫在冰凉的石板地上，一跳一跳地快速穿过。

abstract.en: Picture a squirrel spiralling up a trunk in short bursts.
abstract.cn: 想象一只松鼠贴着树干，一小段一小段地往上蹿。

examples.en: The puppy scampered around the garden all morning.
examples.cn: 小狗整个上午都在花园里又跑又跳。

examples.en: A lizard scampered across the path and vanished into the grass.
examples.cn: 一只蜥蜴飞快地跑过小径，钻进草丛不见了。

examples.en: When the bell rang, the pupils scampered out of the classroom.
examples.cn: 铃声一响，学生们一窝蜂地蹦出教室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「死赶跑」——小家伙飞快地赶着跑、一蹦一跳地窜出去。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为与 scamp 同出于日耳曼语中表示「跑」的词干（属重构形式），英语中约十六世纪后期出现，最初指「匆忙乱跑」，后来收窄为「轻快的碎步蹦跑」。

sensesIntro.en: Scamper describes a run made of small bouncing steps, and from that come running off in fright, climbing in short bursts, and the noun for the sound.
sensesIntro.cn: scamper 描述的是一连串小而弹跳的步子；由此延伸出受惊跑开、分段向上攀爬，以及指称跑动声的名词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small feet hit the ground four or five times very quickly and the animal is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：小脚砸地四五下，动物已经不见了。

branches.en: A child crossing the lawn is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 孩子跑过草坪，这是最日常的义项。

branches.en: A cat leaving at the slam of a gate is the frightened sense.
branches.cn: 门一响猫就跑开，这是受惊的义项。

branches.en: A squirrel reaching the top of a tree is the climbing sense.
branches.cn: 松鼠蹿到树顶，这是向上攀爬的义项。

branches.en: The same light step can be seen and heard, as verb and as noun.
branches.cn: 同一种轻快的步子，既能看见，也能听见，于是分属动词与名词。

branches.en: Both running off and running up rely on short, fast bursts of movement.
branches.cn: 跑开与往上窜都靠短促快速的连环动作。

intro.en: Scamper has no settled deconstruction, so the items below mix its claim of a Germanic stem with the English endings that grow its family.
intro.cn: scamper 没有公认的拆解方式，因此下面的条目把「日耳曼词干」这一存疑说法与衍生词族的英语词尾并列。

latinIntro.en: Scamper has no reliable Latin ancestor; the Germanic stem is a reconstruction and is listed for reference only.
latinIntro.cn: scamper 没有可靠的拉丁语祖先；日耳曼词干属重构形式，这里只作参考列出。

items.example: The stem scamp- is proposed rather than attested.
items.exampleCN: 词干 scamp- 属于拟测而未见文献记录。

items.meaning: to run with light quick steps
items.example: Scamper carries the core running sense.
items.exampleCN: scamper 承载了核心的奔跑含义。

items.example: The noun scamper names one burst of movement.
items.exampleCN: 名词 scamper 指一阵跑动。

items.meaningCN: 构成名词与形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms scampering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 scampering。

items.example: Scampering describes the moving feet.
items.exampleCN: scampering 形容跑动中的脚步。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms scamperer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 scamperer。

items.example: Scamperer names the one who runs.
items.exampleCN: scamperer 指跑动的那一方。

items.example: Scamp is a likely relative with a separate sense.
items.exampleCN: scamp 很可能是同源词，但词义已分开。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms scampered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 scampered。

definition_zh: 扫描仪；扫描器；扫描装置；扫读的人
definition_en: a device that copies a picture or document into a computer, or one that reads data such as light, sound, or a barcode
core_image: 一道细光带贴着一张纸缓缓移过，纸上的字被一格一格读进机器
scene: 图书馆的机器上，学生把借书证贴到玻璃面板前，红灯一闪。He put the receipt on the scanner and clicked scan.
sceneCN: 这里 scanner 是「扫描仪」（第 1 个义项：把纸质文件或图片逐行读进电脑的设备）；句意：他把小票放在扫描仪上，点了「扫描」。可辨识画面：贴在面板前的小票、闪过的红光、屏幕上的预览图。

pos.zh: 扫描仪；扫描器；扫描装置

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「扫描；细看；粗略地看」
由 scan 加 -ing 构成，义为「扫描；扫视」，也指光学扫描的过程
由 scan 加 -able 构成，义为「可扫描的」，指能被机器读入的
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已扫描的；经过扫掠的」

senses.title: A device that copies paper into a computer
senses.definition: a machine that turns a printed page or a photograph into a digital image by passing over it line by line
senses.definitionCN: 逐行扫过纸面或照片、把它们变成数字图像的机器
senses.example: Save the signed contract to the scanner folder.
senses.exampleCN: 把签好的合同存到扫描仪对应的文件夹里。
senses.why: The word is the tool of scanning, so the paper copy becomes its everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「扫描」这个动作的工具，把纸面复制成数字文件自然成了它最日常的义项。

senses.title: A device that reads data from an object
senses.definition: an instrument that reads coded information such as a barcode, a fingerprint, or a code on a card
senses.definitionCN: 读取条码、指纹或卡片编码等信息的装置
senses.example: The scanner refused to read the wet barcode.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描器读不出被弄湿的条形码。
senses.why: Codes carry information in fine lines, so a beam reads them line by line in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 条码把信息藏进细密的线条里，于是用光束一行行读取，与复印纸面的方式一脉相承。

senses.title: An instrument that sweeps a signal
senses.definition: a medical or scientific instrument that sends out light, sound, or radio waves and builds a picture from what returns
senses.definitionCN: 发出光、声或无线电波并依据回波成像的医疗或科研仪器
senses.example: The scanner produced a clear picture of the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描仪拍出了清晰的大脑影像。
senses.why: The same sweep can use sound or radio waves instead of light, which widens the machine to hospitals.
senses.whyCN: 同样的扫掠动作可以改用声波或无线电波代替光，机器于是进入医院，成为影像设备。

senses.title: A person who reads text quickly
senses.definition: a reader who looks through text quickly and selectively rather than word by word
senses.definitionCN: 不逐字而是快速、有选择地浏览文字的人
senses.example: A speed reader is a practised scanner of headlines.
senses.exampleCN: 速读者是熟手，能把标题一扫而过。
senses.why: A person who skims a page is also a scanner of it, since the eye sweeps instead of climbing every word.
senses.whyCN: 一个快速浏览书页的人也在对页面施行扫描，因为眼睛是扫过去的，而不是逐字攀登。

intro.en: Scanner is the agent noun of scan, whose older sense is to climb up, and whose modern senses come from the idea of sweeping the eyes or a beam across something.
intro.cn: scanner 是 scan 的施动名词；scan 的旧义是攀爬，现代各义项则来自「把目光或光束扫过某物」这一意象。

items.en: Scandere means to climb or mount up, as legs climb stairs.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀登、往上走，就像双腿一级一级上楼梯。

items.en: Scansion describes climbing, and the verb survives mainly in verse.
items.cn: scansion 指攀爬，这个词在中古以后主要保留在诗行里。

items.en: To scan a poem is to go through its feet line by line, measuring as you go.
items.cn: 对诗作 scan，就是逐行数它的音步，一边走一边量。

items.en: To scan a page becomes to look over it quickly, the eye moving like a climbing foot.
items.cn: 对书页作 scan，就是飞快看过去，目光像上楼的脚一样移动。

items.en: The technology sense appears, and scanner becomes the machine that scans.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现技术义项，scanner 成为执行扫描的机器。

items.en: Scanner now covers office machines, code readers, and hospital imaging devices.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scanner 涵盖办公机器、读码器与医院影像设备。

note.en: The look-alike group holds scan and its relatives; the near-meaning group holds the other machines that read, copy, or send data.
note.cn: 形近组收 scan 及其同族词；近义组收其余读取、复制或传输数据的设备。

entries.definition: to look over quickly, or to copy with a beam
entries.definitionCN: 义为「扫视；扫描」，是 scanner 的基础动词。

entries.definition: the pattern of stressed and unstressed beats in a verse line
entries.definitionCN: 义为「诗的格律分析」，来自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），与 scan 同源。

entries.definition: to go up
entries.definitionCN: 义为「上升；攀登」，与 scandere 同根，只是拼写与 scanner 相近。

entries.definition: a machine that makes paper copies of documents
entries.definitionCN: 义为「复印机」，输出在纸上，而不是数字文件。

entries.definition: a device that puts text or images onto paper
entries.definitionCN: 义为「打印机」，方向与 scanner 相反，是把数据变成纸面。

entries.definition: a device or person that reads information
entries.definitionCN: 义为「读取器；读者」，范围比 scanner 宽，可指读卡器。

normalIntro.en: Scanner is simply the doer of scan: the thing that moves a beam or an eye across a surface.
normalIntro.cn: scanner 就是做 scan 的那一方：让光束或目光扫过某个表面的东西。

normal.en: The ending -er marks the tool, just as printer marks the printer, so scanner is the tool of scanning.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 表示工具，就像 printer 表示打印机；scanner 就是扫描所用的工具。

normal.en: Flatbed scanner, barcode scanner, and fingerprint scanner show the three main kinds.
normal.cn: 搭配 flatbed scanner、barcode scanner、fingerprint scanner 展示了三类主要设备。

normal.en: The older sense of scan is to climb step by step, which fits a beam that moves line by line.
normal.cn: scan 的旧义是一步步向上爬，这恰好对上逐行移动的光束。

normal.en: Compare printer and copier: a scanner reads in, the other two put out.
normal.cn: 对比 printer 与 copier：scanner 把信息读进来，另两个把信息送出去。

normal.en: To scan a page for one name is to sweep the eyes quickly, the human form of the machine.
normal.cn: 在书页上扫一遍找一个名字，就是人版的扫描。

abstract.en: Picture a thin strip of light sliding down a page in a library booth.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆的隔间里，一道细光带顺着纸面往下滑。

abstract.en: Picture a red beam striking a supermarket barcode and a price appearing.
abstract.cn: 想象超市里红光打在条形码上，价格立刻跳出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hospital ring humming round a patient and a picture forming inside.
abstract.cn: 想象医院里一个圆环绕着病人发出低鸣，影像在屏幕上成形。

examples.en: Please place each page on the scanner with the text facing down.
examples.cn: 请把每页纸文字朝下放到扫描仪上。

examples.en: The airport scanners can see through the closed case.
examples.cn: 机场扫描仪能看穿封闭的箱子。

examples.en: Our office bought a new scanner that handles whole books.
examples.cn: 我们办公室买了一台能处理整本书的新型扫描仪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「死干呢」——机器里的光带贴着纸面一路死干，一行一行把人看不见的东西读进电脑。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 scandere（攀登）→ 晚期拉丁语与古法语 → 英语 scan（数诗的音步；扫视）→ 加表工具与施动者的词尾 -er 构成 scanner，核心义「把光束或目光扫过某物、逐行读取」。

sensesIntro.en: Scanner starts from the act of sweeping across a surface and spreads to the machines that copy paper, read codes, and sweep signals, and finally to a person who reads quickly.
sensesIntro.cn: scanner 从「扫过某个表面」这个动作出发，扩展到复印纸面、读取编码与扫掠信号的几种机器，最后还可以指快速浏览的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow band of light travels across a sheet and the paper turns into data.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道细光带贴着纸面移过，纸上的内容变成数据。

branches.en: A page of text going into a computer is the office sense.
branches.cn: 一页文字进入电脑，这是办公场景义项。

branches.en: A red beam on a barcode is the code-reading sense.
branches.cn: 红光打在条形码上，这是读码义项。

branches.en: A ring humming round a patient is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 圆环绕着病人低鸣，这是医学影像义项。

branches.en: A machine and a person both pass over the surface quickly rather than studying it word by word.
branches.cn: 机器和人都是快速扫过表面，而不是逐字细读。

branches.en: Barcode readers and hospital devices both send out a signal and read what comes back.
branches.cn: 读码器与医院设备都先发出信号，再读取返回的部分。

intro.en: Scanner is built on scan with the agent suffix -er, and the Latin stem scand- shows what scanning meant before it meant copying.
intro.cn: scanner 由 scan 加施动词尾 -er 构成；拉丁词干 scand- 揭示了 scan 在「复制」之前的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandere means to climb, and the same stem gives ascend, descend, and scansion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandere 意为攀登，同一词干还构成 ascend、descend 与 scansion。

items.example: Scandere gives the idea of moving step by step.
items.exampleCN: scandere 提供「一级一级移动」的意象。

items.meaning: a climbing, the measuring of verse feet
items.example: Scansion is the classical relative of scan.
items.exampleCN: scansion 是 scan 在古典语中的亲戚。

items.meaning: to look over quickly, to copy with a beam
items.example: Scan keeps both the eye sense and the beam sense.
items.exampleCN: scan 同时保留目光与光束两种含义。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms scanner from scan.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 scan 变成 scanner。

items.meaningCN: 把动词变成名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms scanning.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 scanning。

items.example: The suffix -able forms scanable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 scanable。

items.example: The prefix a- appears in ascend from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: ascend 中的前缀 a- 与同一词干连用。

items.example: Ascend shares the climbing root with scan.
items.exampleCN: ascend 与 scan 共享「攀登」词根。

items.example: Descend is the same stem with a downward prefix.
items.exampleCN: descend 是同一词干加上向下的前缀。

items.example: Scanner names the tool itself.
items.exampleCN: scanner 指工具本身。

latinEntries.meaning: a climbing, a measuring of verse

definition_zh: 少的；不足的；略微的；勉强够的
definition_en: very little, barely enough, or less than is needed
core_image: 一只碗底只剩几粒米，勺子伸进去几乎碰不到东西
scene: 冰箱里只剩下一小块面包，招待客人时主人显得很为难。With only a scant slice of bread in the fridge, the host looked embarrassed.
sceneCN: 这里 scant 是「少的、不足的」（第 1 个义项：数量极少），句意：冰箱里只剩下一小块面包，招待客人时主人显得很为难。

pos.zh: 减少；削减（旧式或文学用法）

derivatives.zh: scant 加副词后缀 -ily 构成，义为「勉强地；稀少地」
scanty 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「不足；稀少」
scant 的旧式变体加 -y，义为「偏少的；过于节俭的」
动词 scant 的过去分词形容词化，义为「被削减的」

senses.title: Very little in amount
senses.definition: existing in an amount that is much smaller than expected or needed
senses.definitionCN: 数量比预期或所需少得多
senses.example: The team received scant funding for the project.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目只得到很少的经费。
senses.why: The core picture is a nearly empty bowl, so scant first names an amount that is far too small.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是见底的碗，所以 scant 首先指远少于所需的量。

senses.title: Barely enough to meet a need
senses.definition: only just enough to serve a purpose, with nothing to spare
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚够用，没有任何余裕
senses.example: We had scant time to catch the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们几乎没时间赶上末班车。
senses.why: From a small amount comes the sense of just covering the need, like a spoon that only barely reaches the last grains.
senses.whyCN: 由「量少」进一步引申为刚好覆盖需求，就像勺子勉强够到碗底最后几粒米。

senses.title: Offering little for something
senses.definition: not giving, showing, or containing much of something specified
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给予、表现或包含得很少
senses.example: He showed scant concern for his neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他对邻居漠不关心。
senses.why: This sense extends the small amount from things to attitudes and attention that a person supplies.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把「量少」从物品扩展到人给予的态度与注意力上。

senses.title: Covered with little clothing
senses.titleCN: 穿得少的；遮盖不多的（较旧用法）
senses.definition: dressed with very little covering, used chiefly of clothing in older texts
senses.definitionCN: 衣着遮盖很少，主要用于较早的文本
senses.example: The scant summer dress was all she owned.
senses.exampleCN: 她只有一条单薄的夏裙。
senses.why: A small piece of cloth is still a small amount, so the word once described clothing that covers very little.
senses.whyCN: 一小块布料也是「少量」，于是这个词也曾用来形容遮盖很少的衣服。

senses.title: To limit or cut short
senses.titleCN: 减少；削减（旧式或文学用法）
senses.definition: to make smaller in amount or supply, chiefly in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 使数量或供应变少，主要用于较早的写作
senses.example: The drought scanted the harvest that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年的干旱使收成变少。
senses.why: The verb turns the adjective inside out: to scant something is to make it scarce, as if emptying the bowl.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把形容词翻转过来：scant 某物就是让它变得稀罕，好像把碗腾空。

intro.en: Scant comes, through Old Norse, from a Germanic root meaning short, few, or small in number; the exact earlier form is uncertain.
intro.cn: scant 经由古诺尔斯语而来，源于日耳曼语词根，意为「短的、少的、数量小的」；更早的词形来源不确定。

items.en: A Germanic base meaning short or few appears in several old languages.
items.cn: 一个意为「短」或「少」的日耳曼语词基出现在多种古语言中。

items.en: Skamt and skammr carry the sense of short and brief.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语的 skamt 与 skammr 带有「短、短暂」的意思。

items.en: Scant enters English from Norse-influenced northern speech in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: scant 在十三世纪从受北欧影响的北方言语进入英语。

items.en: Scant means short in duration as well as small in amount.
items.cn: 在中古英语后期，scant 既指时间短暂，也指数量少。

items.en: The amount sense wins, and scant becomes the standard adjective for not enough.
items.cn: 现代英语中「数量少」的义项胜出，scant 成为表示「不足」的常用形容词。

note.en: Scant sits between the adjective scanty and near-meaning words such as scarce, sparse, and sparse-like minimal.
note.cn: scant 介于形容词 scanty 与 scarce、sparse、minimal 等近义词之间，核心都是「少」。

entries.definition: small in amount and barely enough
entries.definitionCN: 偏少的；勉强的（由 scant 加 -y 变来）

entries.definition: in a very small or barely sufficient way
entries.definitionCN: 稀少地；勉强地（由 scant 加 -ily 变来）

entries.definition: the quality of being small or insufficient
entries.definitionCN: 不足；稀少（与 scant 同根）

entries.definition: to spend or use too little
entries.definitionCN: 节省得过头（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: not enough to meet demand
entries.definitionCN: 稀缺的；供不应求的

entries.definition: thinly spread out
entries.definitionCN: 稀少的；稀疏的

entries.definition: as small as possible
entries.definitionCN: 最小的；极少的

entries.definition: large and more than enough
entries.definitionCN: 充足的（与 scant 相反）

normalIntro.en: Scant keeps the old Germanic idea of short: a short supply, a short glance, a short allowance.
normalIntro.cn: scant 保留日耳曼语「短」的旧义：供应短、时间短、给予短，都是「少」。

normal.en: Scant attention means people barely look at something.
normal.cn: scant attention 表示人们几乎不怎么关注某事。

normal.en: Scant evidence leaves a case weak.
normal.cn: 证据不足会让案子站不住脚。

normal.en: Scant regard for rules shows careless behaviour.
normal.cn: 对规则几乎不予理会，说明行为草率。

normal.en: The adverb scantily and the noun scantiness both grow from the same root.
normal.cn: 副词 scantily 与名词 scantiness 都由同一词根长成。

normal.en: Compare scanty: scant often sits before abstract nouns, scanty before concrete supplies.
normal.cn: 对比 scanty：scant 多接抽象名词，scanty 多接具体物资。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl holding only a few grains of rice.
abstract.cn: 想象碗里只剩几粒米。

abstract.en: Imagine a spoon scraping the bottom of a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象勺子刮着锅底的声音。

abstract.en: Think of a teacher who barely nods at a careless answer.
abstract.cn: 想象老师对敷衍的回答只勉强点一下头。

examples.en: There is scant hope of finding the lost wallet.
examples.cn: 找到丢失钱包的希望很渺茫。

examples.en: The old bridge gets scant maintenance.
examples.cn: 这座老桥几乎得不到维护。

examples.en: She paid scant heed to his warning.
examples.cn: 她对他的警告几乎没当回事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三块」——口袋里只剩三块钱，零花钱少得可怜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺尔斯语 skamt（短的）+ 日耳曼语词基「短、少」→ 中古英语 scant（数量少、时间短）→ 现代英语 scant（不足的），核心义「差一点才够」。

sensesIntro.en: Scant starts with a small amount, then means barely enough, then little offered in an attitude, and finally appears as an old sense of thin clothing and an old verb meaning to cut short.
sensesIntro.cn: scant 先指数量少，再指勉强够用，继而指态度上给予得少，最后还有「衣物单薄」的旧义与「削减」的旧动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nearly empty bowl with only a few grains left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只几乎见底的碗，只剩几粒米。

branches.en: The amount sense is the everyday core.
branches.cn: 数量少是最日常的核心义。

branches.en: Barely enough is the quantity sense taken to its limit.
branches.cn: 勉强够用是数量义推到极限的结果。

branches.en: Little given moves the small amount from goods to attitudes.
branches.cn: 给予得少把数量从物品转移到态度。

branches.en: Thin clothing is an old concrete application of a small amount of cloth.
branches.cn: 衣料单薄是「少量布料」的古老具体应用。

branches.en: The old verb names the action of making something small.
branches.cn: 旧动词义指出「使某物变少」的动作。

intro.en: Scant is a short Germanic word with a small family: scanty, scantily, scantiness, and a rare verb scanting.
intro.cn: scant 是简短的日耳曼语词，词族不大：scanty、scantily、scantiness，以及少见的动词形式 scanting。

latinIntro.en: Scant has no Latin ancestor; it came from Old Norse, so the Latin family below is empty.
latinIntro.cn: scant 没有拉丁语祖先，它来自古诺尔斯语，因此下面没有拉丁同源词。

items.example: The old sense short in time survives in scant notice.
items.exampleCN: 「时间短」的旧义仍保留在 scant notice 里。

items.example: Scant describes a supply that nearly runs out.
items.exampleCN: scant 描述几乎耗尽的供应。

items.example: The verb is old but still readable in poetry.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词虽旧，诗歌中仍可见到。

items.example: The suffix -y forms scanty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 scanty。

items.example: The suffix -ily forms scantily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ily 构成 scantily。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms scantiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 scantiness。

items.example: Scantily describes how little there is.
items.exampleCN: scantily 描述数量之少。

items.example: Scantiness names the state of being short.
items.exampleCN: scantiness 指不足的状态。

items.example: Scanty often modifies concrete supplies.
items.exampleCN: scanty 常修饰具体物资。

definition_zh: 风景优美的；景色宜人的；与布景有关的
definition_en: having beautiful natural views, or related to the painted setting of a stage
core_image: 一条盘山公路，车窗外是层层叠叠的青山与云雾
scene: 旅行者沿着海边公路开了一整天，每隔几分钟就忍不住停车拍照。The travellers stopped again and again on the scenic coastal road.
sceneCN: 这里 scenic 是「风景优美的」（第 1 个义项：景色美丽），句意：旅行者沿着风景优美的海滨公路开开停停，一次次下车拍照。

pos.zh: 风景优美的；景色宜人的

derivatives.zh: scene 加集合名词后缀 -ery 构成，义为「（总的）风景；舞台布景」
scenic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「在风景方面」
scenic 的基础名词，义为「场景；景色；舞台一幕」
与 scenic 语义相近的独立形容词，义为「如画的；风景秀丽的」（非同一词根）

senses.title: Having beautiful natural views
senses.definition: having or providing attractive natural views, especially of land, water, or sky
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或呈现迷人的自然景色，尤指山水与天空
senses.example: The village is famous for its scenic location.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄以风景优美而闻名。
senses.why: Scenic comes from scene, a view, so the adjective first labels a place whose view is worth looking at.
senses.whyCN: scenic 来自表示「景象」的名词 scene，所以它首先形容一个风景值得一看的地方。

senses.title: Designed for enjoying views
senses.definition: made or arranged so that people can enjoy views along the way
senses.definitionCN: 为让人们沿途欣赏风景而设计或安排的
senses.example: We took the scenic road instead of the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走了观景路线，没有走高速公路。
senses.why: From a beautiful view comes a road, train, or walk chosen because the view is the point.
senses.whyCN: 由「景色美」引申出为看景而选的路线、列车或步道。

senses.title: Of natural scenery in general
senses.titleCN: 自然景物的；风景区性质的
senses.definition: belonging to the natural landscape as a category rather than a single view
senses.definitionCN: 属于自然景观这一类别，而非某一个具体景象
senses.example: The region protects its scenic resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区保护着自身的景观资源。
senses.why: The adjective spreads from one photogenic view to the whole class of landscape features.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从一幅上镜的景象扩展到整类自然景观。

senses.title: Related to stage scenery
senses.definition: relating to the painted setting or backdrops of a theatre stage
senses.definitionCN: 与舞台的绘画布景或背景幕有关的
senses.example: The scenic designer painted a forest backdrop.
senses.exampleCN: 布景设计师画了一幅森林背景。
senses.why: This is the oldest technical use: the scene of a stage, painted and arranged.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的技术用法：舞台上的「一幕场景」，被绘制并布置出来。

senses.title: Attractively presented or arranged
senses.titleCN: 布景般漂亮的；布置得好看的（引申）
senses.definition: arranged so as to be visually impressive, as if set for a picture
senses.definitionCN: 布置得极具视觉吸引力，仿佛为拍照而设
senses.example: The dinner table looked almost scenic.
senses.exampleCN: 晚餐的餐桌几乎像布景一样漂亮。
senses.why: If a view can be arranged on a stage, anything arranged for the eye can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然景色能像舞台一样被布置，那么任何为视觉而安排的东西都能借用这个词。

intro.en: Scenic is built from scene, from Greek skene, the tent or hut behind a stage, plus the adjective suffix -ic.
intro.cn: scenic 由 scene 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成；scene 源自希腊语 skene，指舞台后的帐篷或小屋。

items.en: Skene means a tent, hut, or the booth where actors changed.
items.cn: skene 意为帐篷、小屋，或演员换装的棚子。

items.en: Scena names the stage and its painted setting.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scena 指舞台及其绘画布景。

items.en: Scene reaches English through Old French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: scene 在十四世纪经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: Scenic appears first in theatre talk about painted stage settings.
items.cn: scenic 最早出现在戏剧用语中，指绘制的舞台布景。

items.en: Travel and landscape painting spread the word to natural views.
items.cn: 旅行与风景画把这个词扩展到自然风光上。

note.en: Scenic shares its root with scene and scenery, and stands close to picturesque, breathtaking, and plain.
note.cn: scenic 与 scene、scenery 同根，并与 picturesque、breathtaking 以及反义的 plain 相对。

entries.definition: a place of action or a view
entries.definitionCN: 场景；景象；现场（scenic 的词根）

entries.definition: the landscape of a region, or stage sets
entries.definitionCN: 风景（总称）；舞台布景

entries.definition: as far as the view is concerned
entries.definitionCN: 就风景而言（scenic 的副词形式）

entries.definition: not a real word; a common misspelling of scenic
entries.definitionCN: 不是真实词汇，是 scenic 的常见错拼，注意字母 c 与 n 的先后

entries.definition: attractive in a charming, old-fashioned way
entries.definitionCN: 如画的；古雅秀丽的

entries.definition: extremely impressive to look at
entries.definitionCN: 极其动人的；美得惊人的

entries.definition: offering a wide unbroken view
entries.definitionCN: 全景的；视野开阔的

entries.definition: dull and without beauty
entries.definitionCN: 单调乏味的；无景致的（与 scenic 相反）

normalIntro.en: Scenic is simply scene plus -ic: wherever the scenery is worth stopping for, the adjective fits.
normalIntro.cn: scenic 就是 scene 加 -ic：凡是叫人愿意停车的风景，都能用这个形容词。

normal.en: A scenic route is chosen for its views, not its speed.
normal.cn: scenic route 是为看景而选，不为赶速度。

normal.en: Scenic beauty describes what a camera wants to catch.
normal.cn: scenic beauty 描述的是镜头想要捕捉的美。

normal.en: Scenery is the total landscape, while a scene is one view.
normal.cn: scenery 是总的风景，scene 是一处景象。

normal.en: The scenic designer works in a theatre, not in the mountains.
normal.cn: scenic designer 工作在剧院里，不在山里。

normal.en: Spell it sc-e-nic: the n follows the c, unlike scene.
normal.cn: 拼写是 sc-e-nic：n 跟在 c 之后，与 scene 不同。

abstract.en: Picture a bus window sliding past layer after layer of green hills.
abstract.cn: 想象车窗缓缓滑过一层又一层的青山。

abstract.en: Imagine a camera shutter clicking at every bend in the road.
abstract.cn: 想象每过一个弯都响起快门声。

abstract.en: Think of a stage backdrop unrolled to show painted mountains.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画着山的舞台背景被放下来。

examples.en: The train takes a scenic route along the valley.
examples.cn: 这趟列车沿着山谷走一条风景优美的路线。

examples.en: Tourists come for the scenic views and the quiet air.
examples.cn: 游客冲着美丽的景色和清新的空气而来。

examples.en: The scenic designer won a prize for the forest set.
examples.cn: 布景设计师凭借森林布景获奖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西尼客」——西边来的游客最爱看风景；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 skene（舞台后的帐篷、棚子）→ 拉丁语 scena（舞台、布景）→ 古法语 scene → 英语 scene（景象、场景）+ 后缀 -ic → scenic（有景致之美的）。

sensesIntro.en: Scenic moves from a single beautiful view to routes made for viewing, to whole landscapes, then back to the painted stage scene that started it.
sensesIntro.cn: scenic 从一处美景出发，扩展到为看景而设的路线与整片景观，最后回到它源头的舞台布景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mountain road with layered green hills outside the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘山公路，车窗外层层青山。

branches.en: A beautiful natural view is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 自然美景是最日常的义项。

branches.en: A route made for views follows from choosing the best-looking path.
branches.cn: 观景路线来自「挑最好看的路走」。

branches.en: Landscape as a category widens one view into a whole region.
branches.cn: 作为类别的景观把单处景色扩展成整个地区。

branches.en: Theatre scenery is the original technical sense.
branches.cn: 舞台布景是最初的技术义项。

branches.en: Anything arranged for the eye borrows the picture-like quality.
branches.cn: 任何为视觉而布置的东西都借用了「如画」的特质。

intro.en: Scenic is scene plus the Latin suffix -ic, and it anchors the family scenery, scenically, and the theatre word scenic designer.
intro.cn: scenic 是 scene 加拉丁前缀来源的后缀 -ic，串起 scenery、scenically 以及戏剧用语 scenic designer。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek skene, borrowed into Latin as scena, meaning a stage or its setting.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语 skene，拉丁语借用为 scena，意为舞台或其布景。

items.example: Skene supplies the stage meaning of scene.
items.exampleCN: skene 提供了 scene 的舞台含义。

items.example: Scena is the Latin form of the Greek word.
items.exampleCN: scena 是这个希腊词的拉丁形式。

items.example: Scene is the noun that scenic grows from.
items.exampleCN: scene 是 scenic 所由生长的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms scenic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 scenic。

items.example: The suffix -ery forms scenery.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ery 构成 scenery。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms scenically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 scenically。

items.example: Scenery covers all the views of a place.
items.exampleCN: scenery 概括一个地方的全部景色。

items.example: Scenic describes places worth a stop.
items.exampleCN: scenic 形容值得驻足的地方。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 舞台的（一般认为经由这一形式影响英语）

definition_zh: 气味；香味；踪迹；察觉；香水
definition_en: a smell, especially a pleasant one, or a trail of smell left by someone or something
core_image: 一只狗低着头，鼻子贴着地面，沿着一条看不见的气味线往前追
scene: 厨房里刚烤好的面包香味飘到客厅，孩子循着味道跑过来。The smell of fresh bread drifted from the kitchen, and the child followed the scent.
sceneCN: 这里 scent 是「气味」（第 1 个义项：可闻到的味道），句意：厨房里新烤面包的香味飘了出来，孩子循着气味跑了过来。

derivatives.zh: scent 加过去分词词尾 -ed 形容词化，义为「有香味的」
scent 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无味的；没有气味的」
动词 scent 的动名词形式，义为「嗅闻；察觉」

senses.title: A smell in the air
senses.definition: a smell given off by something, often a pleasant one
senses.definitionCN: 某物散发出的气味，常指好闻的气味
senses.example: The scent of roses filled the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 玫瑰的香气充满了花园。
senses.why: The core picture is a trail of smell in the air, so scent first names any smell that reaches the nose.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是空气中留下的一条气味线，所以 scent 首先指任何传到鼻子的气味。

senses.title: A trail left by an animal or person
senses.definition: the smell left along a path that another animal or person can follow
senses.definitionCN: 沿路留下的气味，可被其他动物或人循着跟踪
senses.example: The hounds picked up the scent at the river.
senses.exampleCN: 猎犬在河边嗅到了踪迹。
senses.why: A smell in the air becomes a track on the ground: the animal that follows a nose is following a path.
senses.whyCN: 空气中的气味落到地面上就成了路径：循着鼻子追赶的动物其实是在追一条路。

senses.title: A hint or clue detected
senses.definition: a faint sign that something is happening or about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事正在或即将发生的微弱迹象
senses.example: The reporter finally got on the scent of a scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 记者终于嗅到了丑闻的线索。
senses.why: From a physical trail comes the detective sense: a lead that someone can follow toward the truth.
senses.whyCN: 由有形的气味线引申出侦探义：可以循着追向真相的一条线索。

senses.title: To become aware of by smell
senses.definition: to notice something with the nose, or to notice something hidden without clear evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用鼻子觉察，或在证据不明确时察觉出隐藏的事情
senses.example: She scented smoke from the old chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 她闻到了老烟囱冒出的烟味。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: the nose set on the trail and moving toward it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：鼻子锁定气味线，然后向它前进。

senses.title: A pleasant-smelling liquid worn on the body
senses.definition: a sweet-smelling liquid applied to the skin or clothes, more often called perfume today
senses.definitionCN: 涂抹在皮肤或衣服上的香液，如今更常说 perfume
senses.example: He wore a spicy scent for the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 晚宴上他用了一款辛辣味的香水。
senses.why: The smell sense moves from what is in the air to the bottled source that puts a smell on the body.
senses.whyCN: 「气味」义从空气中的味道转到瓶装来源，即把香味带上身体的东西。

intro.en: Scent is a shortened form of Old French sente, from sentir to feel or smell, ultimately from Latin sentire; the spelling grew a silent c to match science.
intro.cn: scent 由古法语 sente 缩略而来，源自动词 sentir（感觉、闻），上溯至拉丁语 sentire；拼写里多加了一个不发音的 c，是受 science 影响的模仿。

items.en: Sentire means to feel, perceive, or sense.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、察觉。

items.en: Sentir means to feel or smell, and sente means a track of smell.
items.cn: 古法语 sentir 意为感觉、闻；sente 意为气味踪迹。

items.en: Scent enters English as a hunting word for a trail hounds follow.
items.cn: 十四、十五世纪时 scent 作为狩猎词进入英语，指猎犬追踪的气味。

items.en: A silent c is added for the look of Latin-derived spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪时为了看起来像拉丁词源的拼写，加了一个不发音的 c。

items.en: The word spreads from trails to general smells and finally to perfume.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词从踪迹扩展到一般气味，最终又指香水。

note.en: Scent is the smell word that keeps the idea of a trail, and it sits beside the verbs smell and sniff and the very different word cent.
note.cn: scent 是带「踪迹」意味的气味词，与动词 smell、sniff 相邻，也常和完全不同的 cent 混淆。

entries.definition: the smallest unit of money in many countries
entries.definitionCN: 分（货币单位）；与 scent 同音但只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the past form of send
entries.definitionCN: send 的过去式；与 scent 同音异义，词源不同

entries.definition: agreement
entries.definitionCN: 同意；与 scent 后半截同音，词源不同

entries.definition: having a pleasant smell
entries.definitionCN: 有香味的（scent 加 -ed 构成）

entries.definition: the quality that you can notice with the nose
entries.definitionCN: 气味；味道（最通用的词）

entries.definition: a smell, often an unpleasant one
